migraine.name: Migraine
migraine.description: A neurological disease causing recurrent attacks of moderate to severe head pain, usually one-sided and throbbing, often accompanied by nausea and sensitivity to light and sound.
migraine.body_mechanism: Your brain triggers a wave of electrical activity that causes blood vessels around the brain — especially the temporal artery at your temple — to swell and inflame. These inflamed vessels press on the trigeminal nerve, which covers your forehead, temples, and eye area, sending intense pain signals. This is why you feel throbbing that pulses with your heartbeat, and why the pain is often one-sided.

why_symptoms.headache_unilateral: The inflammation is stronger on one side, causing that characteristic one-sided pain.
why_symptoms.throbbing: The swollen temporal artery pulses with each heartbeat — that pulsing IS what you feel.
why_symptoms.nausea: The trigeminal nerve connects to the vagus nerve which controls your gut — nerve irritation causes nausea.
why_symptoms.photophobia: Your inflamed brain is hypersensitive — even normal light signals are amplified into pain.
why_symptoms.phonophobia: Same reason — sound vibrations reach an already overloaded nervous system.

immediate: Move to a dark, quiet room right now — remove all light and sound stimulation
Apply a cold pack or cold wet cloth to your forehead or the back of your neck
Drink a large glass of water slowly — dehydration worsens migraines
Take ibuprofen or paracetamol at full dose at the EARLIEST sign — do not wait
Lie still — movement increases the pulsing pain in swollen blood vessels
short_term: Rest completely for the duration of the attack — typically 4 to 72 hours
Avoid screens, bright lights, and loud environments until fully resolved
Eat something light when nausea allows — low blood sugar prolongs the attack
A small cup of coffee or tea early in the attack can help — caffeine constricts vessels
Track everything about this attack in your YoSymptom journal
long_term: Keep a headache diary — log sleep, food, stress, and water intake daily
Maintain consistent sleep and wake times — even on weekends
Never skip meals — drops in blood sugar are a major trigger
Stay well hydrated — aim for 8+ glasses of water daily in Uganda's climate
Identify and avoid your personal triggers using your journal data
If attacks happen more than 3 times a month, see a doctor for preventive medication

see_doctor_if: Headache is the worst of your life — sudden and severe (thunderclap)
Accompanied by fever, stiff neck, or rash — could indicate meningitis
Attacks happen more than 3 times per month
Pain lasts more than 3 days continuously
You experience weakness or numbness on one side of the body
Vision changes do not resolve after the headache ends
migraine.local_context: Migraines are often mistaken for malaria headaches in Uganda. Key difference: malaria headaches come with fever and cyclical chills. Migraine headaches come with light sensitivity and nausea without fever.
home_remedies: Ginger tea — slice fresh ginger, boil 10 minutes, add honey. Reduces inflammation and nausea
Cold compress on the forehead and back of neck
Press firmly on the LI4 pressure point — the fleshy web between thumb and index finger
Peppermint oil applied to temples — dilute with carrier oil first

tension_headache.name: Tension Headache
tension_headache.description: The most common type of headache, caused by muscle tension in the neck, scalp, and jaw. It produces a constant pressure or squeezing sensation, usually on both sides of the head.
tension_headache.body_mechanism: Stress, poor posture, or fatigue causes muscles in your neck, shoulders, and scalp to tighten and contract. This sustained muscle tension compresses nerves and reduces blood flow, creating that characteristic band-like pressure feeling around your head — like wearing a tight hat.

immediate: Take paracetamol or ibuprofen — effective for tension headaches when taken early
Apply heat to the back of your neck and shoulders — relaxes the contracted muscles
Gently stretch your neck — slow side-to-side and forward rotations
Take a break from whatever you were doing — especially screen work
Try slow, deep belly breathing for 5 minutes to lower muscle tension
short_term: Address the stress or posture issue that triggered it
Take a short walk in fresh air — physical movement releases muscle tension
Massage your temples, scalp, and the base of your skull gently
Stay hydrated — even mild dehydration causes tension headaches
long_term: Fix your sitting and screen posture — head aligned over spine, not forward
Take screen breaks every 45 minutes — look away and stretch
Manage stress actively — exercise, rest, and addressing what is causing pressure
Strengthen your neck muscles with gentle daily exercises
Limit caffeine — dependency causes rebound headaches

see_doctor_if: Headaches occur more than 15 days per month
Pain is severe or getting progressively worse over weeks
Headaches wake you from sleep regularly
Pain does not respond to over-the-counter painkillers at all
tension_headache.local_context: Very common in students and office workers in Uganda due to long screen hours, stress, and dehydration in the heat.
home_remedies: Hot shower or warm towel on the neck and shoulders
Peppermint or eucalyptus oil rubbed on temples
Drink 2 large glasses of water immediately
Rest in a quiet room for 20 minutes

malaria.name: Malaria
malaria.description: A serious infectious disease caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted through mosquito bites. A leading cause of illness and death in Uganda. Requires prompt diagnosis and treatment.
malaria.body_mechanism: When an infected mosquito bites you, parasites enter your bloodstream and invade red blood cells. Inside the cells they multiply, then burst out in waves — this is what causes the cyclical fevers and chills. Your immune system's fight against the parasites causes the body aches, headache, and fatigue. Severe malaria can affect the brain, kidneys, and lungs.

immediate: Go to a health facility or clinic TODAY for a rapid malaria test — this is urgent
Do not wait to see if it gets better — malaria progresses quickly
Take paracetamol for the fever to keep temperature controlled while travelling to clinic
Drink plenty of fluids — fever causes rapid dehydration
Do not take anti-malarials without confirming the diagnosis first
short_term: Take the full prescribed course of anti-malarial medication — never stop early
Rest completely — your body is fighting a serious infection
Eat small nutritious meals even if appetite is low — your body needs fuel
Monitor for danger signs and return to hospital immediately if they appear
Sleep under an insecticide-treated mosquito net to prevent reinfection
long_term: Always sleep under a mosquito net — every night
Use mosquito repellent especially in the evenings
Eliminate standing water around your home — breeding grounds for mosquitoes
Wear long sleeves in the evenings when mosquitoes are most active
Test immediately whenever you develop fever — do not assume and self-treat

see_doctor_if: ANY suspected malaria — always needs a test and proper treatment
High fever that does not come down with paracetamol
Difficulty breathing or severe weakness
Confusion, seizures, or loss of consciousness — go to hospital IMMEDIATELY
Vomiting that prevents keeping medication down
Yellow eyes or very dark urine — signs of severe malaria
malaria.local_context: Malaria is extremely common in Uganda, especially during and after rainy seasons. The fever often comes in cycles — high fever, then sweating, then feeling better, then fever again. This cyclical pattern is a strong indicator.
home_remedies: Paracetamol for fever management — do NOT use aspirin for malaria fever
Oral rehydration solution (ORS) to prevent dehydration
Cool (not cold) sponge bath to help bring fever down
Rest and avoid all physical exertion until fully recovered

typhoid.name: Typhoid Fever
typhoid.description: A bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi, spread through contaminated food and water. Common in Uganda. Causes sustained high fever and systemic illness requiring antibiotic treatment.
typhoid.body_mechanism: The bacteria enter your gut, penetrate the intestinal wall, and spread through your lymph nodes into your bloodstream. This is why typhoid fever is sustained — not cyclical like malaria — it stays high because bacteria are continuously in your blood triggering your immune response. The bacteria damage the gut lining, causing abdominal pain and in severe cases, perforation.

immediate: See a doctor today for blood or stool test to confirm typhoid
Do not self-treat — typhoid requires specific antibiotics prescribed by a doctor
Drink only boiled or bottled water while waiting for results
Eat only freshly cooked, well-cooked food — avoid raw vegetables and street food
Take paracetamol for fever while seeking medical care
short_term: Take the full course of antibiotics exactly as prescribed — typically 7-14 days
Maintain strict hand hygiene — wash hands thoroughly before eating
Eat soft, easily digestible foods — rice, boiled yam, bananas, soups
Drink plenty of fluids — oral rehydration salts (ORS) are helpful
Rest completely — typhoid is a systemic illness that requires full rest
long_term: Only drink treated, boiled, or bottled water
Wash hands with soap before every meal and after toilet
Avoid street food and raw salads in areas with poor sanitation
Ensure food is thoroughly cooked and eaten immediately — not stored cooked food
Consider typhoid vaccination as prevention

see_doctor_if: All suspected typhoid cases need medical assessment
Severe abdominal pain — could indicate intestinal perforation (emergency)
Confusion or altered consciousness
Very high fever that does not respond to paracetamol
Bleeding from the gut — blood in stool or vomit
typhoid.local_context: Typhoid is common across Uganda, especially where water supply is unreliable. Key difference from malaria: typhoid fever is SUSTAINED — stays high for days without the cyclical pattern of malaria. Headache in typhoid tends to be frontal and constant.
home_remedies: ORS (oral rehydration salts) — very important to prevent dehydration
Soft BRAT diet — bananas, rice, apples, toast/bread while ill
Paracetamol only for fever — never aspirin or ibuprofen (irritates the gut)
Complete bed rest — do not push through typhoid

hypertension.name: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)
hypertension.description: A condition where blood pressure in the arteries is persistently elevated. Often called the 'silent killer' because most people have no symptoms. However, very high pressure can cause headaches, dizziness, and in crisis, stroke.
hypertension.body_mechanism: Your blood exerts pressure against artery walls with every heartbeat. When this pressure is consistently too high, it damages artery walls over time, forces the heart to work harder, and can rupture small blood vessels — including in the brain. The headache from hypertension is from increased pressure being transmitted to blood vessels in the head.

immediate: Sit down and rest quietly — reduce any physical or emotional stress immediately
If you have a blood pressure monitor, measure your blood pressure now
Do not take headache tablets and assume the problem is solved — see a doctor
Avoid coffee, cigarettes, and any stimulants right now
If you have prescribed blood pressure medication, take it as directed
short_term: See a doctor or nurse to have blood pressure measured — this is the only way to know
Start reducing salt intake — stop adding salt to food
Begin gentle daily walking — even 30 minutes makes a significant difference
Reduce alcohol consumption if applicable
Manage stress actively — identify and address major stress sources
long_term: Take blood pressure medication exactly as prescribed — never stop without doctor advice
Measure blood pressure regularly — many pharmacies offer free checks
Maintain a healthy weight — every kilogram lost reduces blood pressure
Eat more fruits and vegetables, especially potassium-rich foods like bananas
Limit processed and salty foods
Exercise regularly — 30 minutes of walking at least 5 days a week

see_doctor_if: Severe headache, especially at the back of the head, that is new or different
Headache with blurred vision, confusion, or chest pain
Blood pressure reading above 180/120 — this is a hypertensive crisis
Sudden weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking — could be a stroke (call for help NOW)
Any first diagnosis of high blood pressure — needs full assessment
hypertension.local_context: Hypertension is increasingly common in Uganda, especially in urban areas. Many people don't know they have it. If you are over 30 and have never had your blood pressure checked — please do so.
home_remedies: Reduce salt — use herbs and spices for flavour instead
Daily walking — even a 20-minute walk helps significantly
Deep breathing and stress management
Hibiscus tea (Zobo/Sorrel) — has evidence of mild blood pressure reduction

flu.name: Influenza (Flu)
flu.description: A viral respiratory infection causing sudden onset of fever, body aches, cough, and fatigue. More severe than a common cold and can be dangerous in elderly, pregnant women, and those with underlying conditions.
flu.body_mechanism: The influenza virus infects cells lining your respiratory tract. Your immune system launches a powerful response — this is what causes the high fever, intense muscle aches, and profound fatigue. The virus spreads through respiratory droplets when infected people cough, sneeze, or talk.

immediate: Rest completely — this is the most important thing you can do
Take paracetamol for fever and body aches — follow dosing instructions
Drink plenty of warm fluids — water, broth, herbal teas
Stay at home — flu is highly contagious for 5-7 days
Cover your mouth when coughing or sneezing — protect those around you
short_term: Gargle warm salt water for sore throat
Use steam inhalation for congestion — carefully with hot water and a towel
Eat light nutritious food — soups, porridge, fruits
Monitor for worsening — especially breathing difficulty
Most people recover in 7-10 days with good rest and hydration
long_term: Wash hands frequently — especially after coughing and before eating
Avoid close contact with sick people when possible
Maintain good nutrition and sleep — keeps immune system strong
Ventilate your living spaces — fresh air reduces viral transmission

see_doctor_if: Difficulty breathing or chest pain
Confusion or inability to stay awake
Persistent vomiting preventing fluid intake
Fever that returns after seeming to improve — can indicate bacterial complication
Symptoms in a child under 5, pregnant woman, or elderly person
flu.local_context: Flu and malaria can feel similar in the early stages. Key difference: flu does NOT have the cyclical fever pattern of malaria and comes with more respiratory symptoms. If in doubt, test for malaria.
home_remedies: Ginger and honey tea — anti-inflammatory and soothing for throat
Turmeric in warm milk — traditional immune support
Steam inhalation with eucalyptus leaves
Warm salt gargle 3-4 times daily for sore throat

gastritis.name: Gastritis / Peptic Ulcer Disease
gastritis.description: Inflammation of the stomach lining, often caused by the H. pylori bacteria, regular use of painkillers (NSAIDs), or excess stomach acid. Causes burning upper abdominal pain, often related to meals.
gastritis.body_mechanism: Your stomach lining is protected by a layer of mucus. When this protection breaks down — due to bacteria, medication, or acid — the stomach's own acid damages the lining beneath, causing inflammation and ulceration. The burning pain you feel is stomach acid touching exposed, irritated tissue.

immediate: Eat something — even crackers or plain bread — to absorb excess acid
Take an antacid if available — provides quick relief by neutralising acid
Avoid coffee, alcohol, spicy food, and citrus right now — all irritate the lining
Do not take ibuprofen or aspirin — these directly damage the stomach lining
Drink a glass of warm water or milk to help soothe the lining
short_term: Eat smaller meals more frequently instead of large meals
Avoid lying down immediately after eating — sit upright for 1 hour
Stop or reduce NSAIDs (ibuprofen, aspirin, diclofenac) — discuss alternatives with a doctor
Take prescribed medication as directed — proton pump inhibitors are very effective
See a doctor if symptoms persist — H. pylori requires specific antibiotic treatment
long_term: Eat at regular times — an empty stomach produces acid with nothing to neutralise it
Reduce stress — stress increases acid production significantly
Limit coffee, alcohol, and very spicy or fatty foods
If you take regular painkillers, always take them with food or switch to paracetamol
Test for H. pylori bacteria if recurrent — it is the most common cause

see_doctor_if: Vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds
Black, tarry stools — indicates bleeding in the stomach
Severe pain that does not improve with antacids
Unexplained weight loss
Symptoms that persist longer than 2 weeks
gastritis.local_context: Gastritis is very common in Uganda, partly due to high NSAID use (ibuprofen is widely used for malaria-related body aches) and H. pylori, which is prevalent in areas with limited water treatment.
home_remedies: Raw honey — has antibacterial properties against H. pylori
Aloe vera juice — soothes the stomach lining
Banana — coating effect on the stomach lining
Coconut water — alkaline, helps neutralise stomach acid

uti.name: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI)
uti.description: A bacterial infection in any part of the urinary system — kidneys, bladder, or urethra. More common in women. Causes burning urination, frequent urges to urinate, and lower abdominal discomfort.
uti.body_mechanism: Bacteria — usually E. coli from the bowel — travel up the urethra and colonise the bladder. Your immune system responds with inflammation, which is what causes the burning sensation and urgency. Untreated, infection can travel to the kidneys, becoming more serious.

immediate: Drink large amounts of water — flushing the urinary tract helps clear bacteria
Urinate when you feel the urge — do not hold it in
See a doctor today or tomorrow — UTIs need antibiotics
Avoid holding urine for long periods — this allows bacteria to multiply
Paracetamol can help with discomfort while waiting to see a doctor
short_term: Take the full antibiotic course prescribed — typically 3-7 days
Drink at least 2-3 litres of water daily throughout treatment
Avoid coffee, alcohol, and fizzy drinks — these irritate the bladder
Cranberry juice or tablets may help prevent recurrence
long_term: Always wipe front to back after using the toilet
Urinate after sexual activity to flush the urethra
Drink plenty of water daily — concentrated urine encourages bacterial growth
Wear cotton underwear — reduces moisture that encourages bacterial growth
Do not use harsh soaps or douches in the genital area

see_doctor_if: Fever with back pain or side pain — may indicate kidney infection
Blood in urine
Symptoms do not improve after 2-3 days of antibiotics
Recurring UTIs — more than 2 per year
UTI in a man — always needs medical assessment
uti.local_context: Common in Uganda especially in women. Limited water intake due to cost or access worsens the risk. Prompt treatment is important to prevent kidney involvement.
home_remedies: Lots of water — most important remedy
Unsweetened cranberry juice — inhibits bacteria from sticking to bladder walls
Avoid spicy food and coffee which irritate the bladder
Warm compress on lower abdomen for pain relief

anxiety.name: Anxiety / Stress Response
anxiety.description: A state of excessive worry, fear, or nervousness that can cause both psychological and physical symptoms. Very common, highly treatable, and nothing to be ashamed of.
anxiety.body_mechanism: Your brain activates the 'fight or flight' response — releasing adrenaline and cortisol. This speeds up your heart, tightens muscles, quickens breathing, and sharpens senses. In short bursts this is normal and helpful. When it stays activated chronically due to ongoing stress, it causes physical symptoms — chest tightness, headaches, stomach upset, and fatigue.

immediate: Stop what you are doing and breathe — 4 counts in, hold 4, out for 6. Repeat 5 times
Name 5 things you can see, 4 you can touch, 3 you can hear — grounds you in the present
Move your body — even a short walk changes your brain chemistry immediately
Call someone you trust — talking about what you are feeling reduces anxiety's power
Remind yourself: anxiety is your body's alarm system — it is trying to protect you, not harm you
short_term: Identify what is causing the anxiety — name it specifically
Break overwhelming problems into small, actionable steps
Reduce or eliminate caffeine — it directly amplifies anxiety
Prioritise sleep — anxiety and poor sleep reinforce each other
Exercise regularly — one of the most effective anxiety treatments known
long_term: Build a daily stress management practice — prayer, reflection, walks, or journaling
Address underlying causes — relationship, financial, or work stressors need real solutions
Reduce alcohol — it temporarily reduces anxiety but increases it over time
Consider speaking to a counsellor — talking therapy is highly effective
Maintain strong social connections — isolation amplifies anxiety significantly

see_doctor_if: Anxiety is preventing you from functioning at work, school, or in relationships
You are having panic attacks — sudden intense episodes of fear with physical symptoms
You are using alcohol or substances to manage anxiety
You have thoughts of harming yourself — seek help immediately
Anxiety has persisted for more than 2 weeks without improvement
anxiety.local_context: Mental health challenges are real and common in Uganda but often not discussed openly. Anxiety is not weakness or a spiritual problem — it is a health condition with effective treatments. Seeking help is a sign of strength.
home_remedies: Deep breathing exercises — practise daily, not just during anxious moments
Physical exercise — any form, any duration, daily
Reducing caffeine and increasing water intake
Journaling — writing thoughts reduces their intensity

asthma.name: Asthma
asthma.description: A chronic condition where the airways narrow and swell, making breathing difficult. Causes recurring episodes of wheezing, breathlessness, and chest tightness, often triggered by allergens, exercise, or cold air.
asthma.body_mechanism: In asthma, the airways are chronically inflamed. When a trigger is encountered, the muscles around the airways contract (bronchospasm) and the airway lining swells and produces extra mucus. This triple narrowing makes breathing — especially breathing out — much harder, producing the characteristic wheeze.

immediate: Sit upright — do not lie down during an attack as it worsens breathing
Use your reliever inhaler (blue/salbutamol) if you have one — take as prescribed
Stay calm — panic tightens airways further
Remove yourself from the trigger if possible — smoke, dust, cold air
If no improvement after 10 minutes of inhaler use, seek emergency care
short_term: Identify and avoid your personal triggers — dust, smoke, cold air, exercise, etc.
Take your preventer inhaler daily as prescribed — not just during attacks
Keep your living space dust-free — damp-mop rather than sweeping
Use a preventer inhaler before exercise if exercise triggers attacks
See a doctor for a formal asthma action plan
long_term: Never smoke and avoid second-hand smoke completely
Keep a dust-free sleeping environment — use pillow covers
Maintain a healthy weight — obesity worsens asthma significantly
Build aerobic fitness gradually — swimming is particularly good for asthma
Know your warning signs and act early in every attack

see_doctor_if: Severe breathlessness that does not respond to reliever inhaler — go to hospital NOW
Blue lips or fingernails — go to hospital immediately
Speaking in single words because of breathlessness
Attacks are increasing in frequency or severity
First-time symptoms suggestive of asthma — needs formal diagnosis
asthma.local_context: Asthma is increasingly common in Uganda's urban areas due to air pollution, dust from unpaved roads, and indoor cooking smoke. Many people with asthma in Uganda are undiagnosed and untreated.
home_remedies: Steam inhalation with menthol or eucalyptus — opens airways temporarily
Ginger tea — has bronchodilating properties
Reduce exposure to indoor smoke — cook in ventilated spaces
Keep windows open in your home when outdoor air quality is good

cluster_headache.name: Cluster Headache
cluster_headache.description: One of the most painful headache disorders. Causes intense, burning or stabbing pain around one eye, occurring in clusters — multiple attacks per day for weeks, then disappearing for months.
cluster_headache.body_mechanism: Cluster headaches involve the trigeminal nerve and the hypothalamus — the brain's biological clock. The hypothalamus activates the trigeminal nerve pathway in a cyclical pattern, causing the characteristic cluster periods. The pain is so severe because the trigeminal nerve is the main pain nerve of the face and head.

immediate: Sit upright — unlike migraine, lying down worsens cluster headache pain
Get fresh air or breathe oxygen if available — high-flow oxygen is the most effective acute treatment
Stay in a lit room — unlike migraine, darkness does not help cluster headaches
Move around — restlessness is normal and often helps manage the intensity
See a doctor urgently — cluster headaches need prescription treatment
short_term: See a neurologist or doctor for proper diagnosis and treatment
Triptans (sumatriptan injection or nasal spray) are the most effective acute treatments
Keep a headache diary tracking exact timing of attacks — clusters are very predictable
Identify and avoid alcohol completely during cluster periods — it reliably triggers attacks
Establish a consistent sleep schedule — disruption triggers attacks
long_term: Preventive medications (verapamil, lithium) prescribed by doctor reduce cluster frequency
Avoid all alcohol during cluster periods — it is a guaranteed trigger
Maintain consistent sleep patterns year-round
Learn your cluster season — most people have predictable annual cluster periods
High-flow oxygen prescription for home use is highly effective and worth requesting

see_doctor_if: Any suspected cluster headache — needs formal diagnosis and prescription treatment
Pain is preventing you from functioning at all
Attacks are occurring more than 3 times daily
This is your first such headache — emergency causes must be ruled out
cluster_headache.local_context: Cluster headaches are rare but extremely severe. In Uganda, access to high-flow oxygen and triptans may be limited — see a neurologist at a major hospital. The condition is more common in men who smoke.
home_remedies: Fresh air or open window during attack — some relief from increased oxygen
Cold pack firmly pressed against the affected eye area
Capsaicin (hot pepper) nasal drops — traditional remedy with some evidence
Complete avoidance of alcohol — the most important preventive step you can take

malaria_mild.name: Mild Malaria
malaria_mild.description: Uncomplicated malaria — the most common presentation in Uganda. Causes cyclical fever, chills, headache, and fatigue. Treatable with appropriate anti-malarials when caught early.
malaria_mild.body_mechanism: Plasmodium parasites invade your red blood cells and multiply inside them. When the cells burst — releasing the next generation of parasites into your bloodstream — your immune system reacts with a massive inflammatory response. This causes the sudden high fever. The fever then breaks into sweating as your body tries to cool down. This cycle repeats every 48-72 hours depending on the parasite species.

immediate: Test immediately — go to a clinic, pharmacy, or health centre for a rapid malaria test today
Do not self-treat with anti-malarials without confirming the diagnosis first
Take paracetamol for fever while travelling to get tested — do not use aspirin
Drink large amounts of water and ORS — fever causes rapid fluid loss
Note the pattern of your fever — this helps the doctor confirm malaria
short_term: Take the complete prescribed anti-malarial course — never stop early even when feeling better
Rest completely — your body is fighting an infection
Eat nutritious food even if appetite is low — your body needs energy to fight the parasite
Monitor for danger signs and go back to hospital immediately if they appear
Protect others — sleep under a net and reduce mosquito exposure
long_term: Always sleep under an insecticide-treated mosquito net
Apply mosquito repellent especially between dusk and dawn
Eliminate standing water around your home — buckets, tyres, blocked gutters
Wear long sleeves and trousers in the evenings
Test immediately whenever fever occurs — do not delay and do not assume

see_doctor_if: All suspected malaria needs testing and proper treatment — do not delay
Fever above 39°C that does not respond to paracetamol
Any confusion, difficulty breathing, or inability to stand
Yellow eyes or very dark (coca-cola coloured) urine
Vomiting that prevents keeping medication or fluids down
malaria_mild.local_context: Malaria is the leading cause of illness in Uganda. The rainy seasons (March-May and October-December) see the highest transmission. Prompt testing and treatment is critical — most malaria deaths occur because treatment was delayed.
home_remedies: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) — most important — prevents dangerous dehydration
Paracetamol only for fever — not aspirin or ibuprofen
Cool (not cold) sponge bath to bring fever temperature down
Complete bed rest — do not push through malaria

sinusitis.name: Sinusitis
sinusitis.description: Inflammation of the sinuses — air-filled cavities in the skull around the nose and eyes. Causes facial pain and pressure, nasal congestion, and sometimes headache. Usually triggered by a cold or allergies.
sinusitis.body_mechanism: Your sinuses normally drain mucus through small openings into your nasal passages. When these openings become blocked — due to inflammation from infection or allergy — mucus builds up inside the sinus cavities. The trapped mucus becomes a breeding ground for bacteria. The pressure from this trapped fluid is what causes the characteristic facial pain and the headache that worsens when you bend over.

immediate: Steam inhalation — lean over a bowl of hot water with a towel over your head for 10 minutes
Nasal saline rinse — dissolve half teaspoon of salt in warm boiled water and rinse each nostril
Stay well hydrated — thin mucus drains more easily than thick mucus
Apply a warm compress to your face over the painful sinuses
Ibuprofen for pain — it also reduces inflammation in the sinus lining
short_term: Continue steam inhalation 3-4 times daily until symptoms clear
Sleep with your head slightly elevated — helps sinus drainage
Avoid cold air and sudden temperature changes which constrict sinuses
If no improvement after 7-10 days, see a doctor — may need antibiotics
Antihistamines if allergies are the trigger
long_term: Identify and manage allergy triggers — dust, pollen, mould
Use a saline nasal rinse regularly during allergy season
Keep your home well ventilated and dust-free
Treat colds promptly before they turn into sinusitis
Stay hydrated year-round — thin mucus prevents blockage

see_doctor_if: Severe headache or facial pain not relieved by painkillers
High fever with sinusitis — may indicate bacterial infection needing antibiotics
Symptoms persisting more than 10-14 days without improvement
Vision changes or swelling around the eyes — rare but serious complication
Recurrent sinusitis more than 4 times per year
sinusitis.local_context: Sinusitis is common in Kampala due to dust from unpaved roads, vehicle exhaust, and the transition between rainy and dry seasons causing rapid temperature and humidity changes.
home_remedies: Steam with eucalyptus leaves or drops — opens sinuses effectively
Warm ginger tea — anti-inflammatory and helps thin mucus
Salt water nasal rinse — clears mucus and reduces inflammation
Warm face compress — relieves facial pressure and pain

back_pain.name: Lower Back Pain
back_pain.description: Pain in the lower back affecting the muscles, ligaments, nerves, or bones of the lumbar spine. Extremely common — one of the leading causes of disability worldwide. Most cases resolve with appropriate care.
back_pain.body_mechanism: Your lower back bears the full weight of your upper body and acts as the pivot point for nearly every movement. When the muscles, ligaments, or discs that support the lumbar spine become strained or inflamed, they cause pain. Nerve compression from a disc pressing on the sciatic nerve can send pain down the leg — this is sciatica.

immediate: Rest in a comfortable position — on your back with knees bent, or on your side with a pillow between knees
Apply ice pack for first 48 hours — 20 minutes on, 20 off — reduces acute inflammation
After 48 hours switch to heat — warm compress or hot water bottle relaxes muscle spasm
Take ibuprofen — both pain relief and anti-inflammatory effect
Avoid bed rest beyond 1-2 days — staying still worsens back pain
short_term: Gentle movement is better than rest — short walks help recovery
Avoid bending, heavy lifting, and twisting during recovery
Sleep on a firm surface — mattresses that sag worsen back pain
Apply heat for 20 minutes before activity to loosen muscles
See a doctor or physiotherapist if no improvement after 2 weeks
long_term: Strengthen your core muscles — planks, bridges, and gentle abdominal exercises
Maintain good posture especially when sitting for long periods
When lifting — bend your knees, keep the object close, never twist while lifting
Maintain a healthy weight — every extra kilogram strains the lower back
Regular walking and swimming are the best exercises for back health

see_doctor_if: Severe pain that does not improve with rest or painkillers
Pain down the leg below the knee — especially with numbness or weakness
Loss of bladder or bowel control — emergency, go immediately
Back pain with fever — could indicate spinal infection
Pain that started after a significant fall or accident
Pain that wakes you from sleep regularly
back_pain.local_context: Back pain is very common in Uganda among people who do manual labour, carry heavy loads on their head, and those with sedentary desk or boda-boda work. Posture during long journeys on public transport is also a common trigger.
home_remedies: Warm compress or hot water bottle on the lower back
Gentle stretching — child's pose, knee-to-chest stretches
Turmeric in warm milk — natural anti-inflammatory
Massage with warm coconut or sesame oil — loosens muscle spasm

depression.name: Depression
depression.description: A mood disorder causing persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest that interfere with daily life. A real medical condition — not a character weakness or spiritual failure. Highly treatable.
depression.body_mechanism: Depression involves changes in brain chemistry — particularly serotonin, dopamine, and norepinephrine — the neurotransmitters that regulate mood, motivation, and pleasure. The brain's prefrontal cortex (responsible for decision-making and positive emotion) becomes underactive while the amygdala (the fear centre) becomes overactive. This creates the characteristic combination of low mood, hopelessness, and inability to feel pleasure.

immediate: Tell someone you trust how you are feeling — isolation makes depression worse
Do one small physical activity today — even a 10 minute walk has an immediate effect on mood
Avoid making major life decisions while in a depressive episode — your judgment is temporarily affected
Remove or reduce alcohol — it is a depressant that significantly worsens depression
If you are having thoughts of harming yourself — tell someone immediately and seek help
short_term: See a doctor, counsellor, or mental health professional — depression responds well to treatment
Exercise regularly — 30 minutes 5 times a week is as effective as antidepressants for mild-moderate depression
Maintain a daily routine — depression thrives in unstructured time
Eat regularly even when appetite is low — blood sugar affects mood significantly
Get sunlight exposure daily — particularly important in overcast conditions
long_term: Talking therapy (counselling) is highly effective — even a few sessions make a difference
If prescribed antidepressants, take them consistently for at least 4-6 weeks before expecting full effect
Build strong social connections — depression is amplified by isolation
Address underlying stressors — financial, relationship, or work problems need real solutions
Develop a relapse prevention plan with your doctor after recovering

see_doctor_if: Thoughts of suicide or self-harm — seek help immediately, today
Unable to function at work, school, or in relationships
Symptoms lasting more than 2 weeks
Using alcohol or substances to manage the feelings
Physical symptoms like unexplained pain or weight loss alongside low mood
depression.local_context: Depression is common in Uganda but heavily stigmatised. Many people suffer in silence for years. It is not weakness, laziness, or spiritual failure — it is a medical condition with effective treatments. Seeking help is an act of courage. Counselling is available at most major hospitals.
home_remedies: Daily physical exercise — any form, consistently — is one of the most evidence-backed treatments
Sunlight exposure — sit outside in morning light for 20 minutes daily
Social connection — make the effort to be with people even when you don't feel like it
Journaling thoughts — externalising thoughts reduces their emotional weight

food_poisoning.name: Food Poisoning / Gastroenteritis
food_poisoning.description: Illness caused by eating contaminated food or water containing bacteria, viruses, or toxins. Causes sudden onset of nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, and stomach cramps. Usually self-limiting but dehydration is the main danger.
food_poisoning.body_mechanism: When harmful bacteria (Salmonella, E. coli, Staphylococcus) or viruses enter your gut, your digestive system tries to expel them as fast as possible. Vomiting clears the stomach and diarrhoea rushes pathogens out of the intestines. This protective response also causes rapid fluid and electrolyte loss — the main danger of food poisoning is dehydration, not the pathogen itself.

immediate: Start oral rehydration immediately — mix 1 litre of clean water + 6 teaspoons sugar + 1/2 teaspoon salt
Sip the ORS solution slowly and continuously — small sips prevent triggering vomiting
Rest completely — your body is using all its energy to fight the infection
Do not eat solid food until vomiting stops — then start with plain rice, bread, or banana
Avoid anti-diarrhoea tablets in the first 24 hours — diarrhoea is expelling the pathogen
short_term: Continue ORS until diarrhoea stops completely
Eat the BRAT diet — Bananas, Rice, boiled Apples, Toast/bread
Avoid dairy, fatty foods, coffee, and alcohol until fully recovered
Wash hands thoroughly — food poisoning spreads easily in households
Discard any leftover food that may have caused the illness
long_term: Only drink treated, boiled, or bottled water
Wash hands with soap before cooking, before eating, and after toilet
Cook meat thoroughly — especially chicken and minced meat
Refrigerate cooked food promptly — do not leave cooked food at room temperature for hours
Avoid street food where food handling standards are uncertain

see_doctor_if: Unable to keep any fluids down for more than 6 hours
Signs of dehydration — dry mouth, no urination, sunken eyes, severe weakness
Blood in vomit or diarrhoea
High fever (above 39°C) with food poisoning
Symptoms in a young child, elderly person, or pregnant woman
No improvement after 2-3 days
food_poisoning.local_context: Food poisoning is extremely common in Uganda due to water quality issues, lack of refrigeration, and food handling in hot conditions. Street food and reheated food are common sources. ORS powder is available at all pharmacies and health centres.
home_remedies: Homemade ORS — 1L water + 6 teaspoons sugar + 1/2 teaspoon salt
Ginger tea — reduces nausea significantly
Banana — gentle on the gut and replaces lost potassium
Coconut water — natural electrolyte replacement

hypertensive_headache.name: Hypertensive Headache
hypertensive_headache.description: A headache caused by dangerously high blood pressure (hypertensive crisis). Usually felt at the back of the head and neck, often with a pounding quality. Requires immediate medical attention.
hypertensive_headache.body_mechanism: When blood pressure reaches crisis levels (usually above 180/120mmHg), the increased pressure is transmitted to blood vessels in the brain. Small vessels in the brain can rupture or leak, and the brain tissue itself can swell. The headache at the back of the head is caused by pressure on the blood vessels and meninges in that region — this is a warning sign that the brain is under dangerous pressure.

immediate: Sit down immediately and rest completely — do not exert yourself at all
If you have a blood pressure monitor, check it now
Take your prescribed blood pressure medication if you have it
Go to a clinic or hospital today — do not wait to see if it gets better
Do not drive yourself — ask someone to take you or call for help
short_term: Get your blood pressure measured immediately at a clinic
Do not eat salty food, drink coffee, or smoke — all raise blood pressure further
Stay calm — anxiety raises blood pressure further
If prescribed medication, take it exactly as directed from now on — never skip
Return for follow-up in 48 hours to confirm blood pressure has normalised
long_term: Take blood pressure medication every day without exception
Reduce salt to an absolute minimum in your diet
Daily walking for at least 30 minutes significantly reduces blood pressure
Lose weight if overweight — every kilogram matters
Manage stress — chronically high stress drives chronically high blood pressure

see_doctor_if: Headache at the back of the head with known high blood pressure — go today
Severe headache with blurred vision — could be hypertensive emergency
Chest pain or difficulty breathing with headache
Any sudden severe headache in a person with high blood pressure
Weakness, confusion, or difficulty speaking — possible stroke, go immediately
hypertensive_headache.local_context: Hypertension is increasingly common in Uganda, particularly in urban areas and among people over 40. Many people do not know their blood pressure is dangerously high. If you have never had your blood pressure checked and are over 30, please do so — it could save your life.
home_remedies: Complete rest in a calm environment immediately
Hibiscus tea (Zobo) — mild blood pressure lowering effect, safe to use
Avoid all salt, coffee, and stimulants
Deep slow breathing — activates the parasympathetic nervous system, lowering blood pressure

conjunctivitis.name: Conjunctivitis (Pink Eye)
conjunctivitis.description: Inflammation of the thin membrane covering the white of the eye and inside of eyelids. Causes redness, itching, discharge, and a gritty feeling. Can be viral, bacterial, or allergic.
conjunctivitis.body_mechanism: The conjunctiva — the transparent membrane covering your eye — becomes infected or irritated. In viral and bacterial conjunctivitis, the immune response causes the blood vessels in the conjunctiva to dilate (making the eye red) and increases mucus production (causing discharge). In allergic conjunctivitis, histamine release causes intense itching and watering.

immediate: Wash your hands — conjunctivitis is highly contagious
Clean discharge from eye with clean cotton wool or cloth moistened with clean water — wipe outward
Do not touch or rub your eyes — it worsens irritation and spreads infection
Remove contact lenses if worn — do not put them back until fully recovered
Do not share towels, pillowcases, or face cloths with others
short_term: Warm compress on the eye — gently loosens crusting and reduces discomfort
Antibiotic eye drops from pharmacy for bacterial conjunctivitis — use full course
Antihistamine drops or tablets for allergic conjunctivitis
Rest eyes from screens as much as possible
Viral conjunctivitis clears on its own in 7-14 days with supportive care
long_term: Wash hands frequently — especially before touching face and eyes
Avoid sharing eye makeup, towels, or pillows
If recurrent allergic conjunctivitis — identify and reduce exposure to triggers
Clean contact lenses properly and replace regularly

see_doctor_if: Severe pain in the eye — not just irritation
Significant vision changes or blurring that does not clear with blinking
Very intense redness with thick pus — may need prescription antibiotics
Newborn baby with eye discharge — always needs medical assessment
No improvement after 7-10 days of treatment
conjunctivitis.local_context: Conjunctivitis spreads very easily, especially in schools and workplaces. Viral outbreaks are common in Uganda. The key sign of bacterial vs viral: bacterial produces thick, coloured discharge while viral produces watery discharge.
home_remedies: Warm clean water compress 3-4 times daily
Rose water — traditional soothing eye wash (use only if very clean)
Honey dissolved in warm boiled water — ancient antibacterial eye wash (use carefully)
Avoid smoke and dusty environments which irritate inflamed eyes

palpitations.name: Heart Palpitations
palpitations.description: An awareness of your own heartbeat — feeling it racing, pounding, fluttering, or skipping beats. Often harmless but sometimes indicates an underlying heart condition that needs assessment.
palpitations.body_mechanism: Normally you are not aware of your heartbeat. Palpitations occur when the heart beats irregularly, too fast, too hard, or the nervous system is hypersensitive to normal beats. The most common cause is an extra heartbeat (ectopic beat) which is usually completely harmless. Anxiety, caffeine, dehydration, and anaemia are common non-cardiac causes.

immediate: Sit or lie down calmly — most palpitations resolve on their own within minutes
Try the Valsalva manoeuvre — hold your nose, close your mouth, and bear down as if straining. This can reset the heart rhythm
Splash cold water on your face — activates the vagus nerve and can slow heart rate
Avoid caffeine, energy drinks, and stimulants — common triggers
Breathe slowly — 4 counts in, 6 counts out. Prevents hyperventilation which worsens palpitations
short_term: Keep a log of when palpitations occur — before/after meals, during stress, at rest
Reduce or eliminate caffeine — tea, coffee, energy drinks, sodas
Stay well hydrated — dehydration is a common cause
Avoid alcohol — it commonly triggers palpitations
Get your haemoglobin checked — anaemia is a common cause in Uganda
long_term: See a doctor for an ECG — a simple heart tracing identifies most significant arrhythmias
Manage anxiety — the most common cause of persistent palpitations
Regular moderate exercise actually strengthens the heart and reduces ectopic beats
Maintain electrolyte balance — potassium and magnesium are particularly important for heart rhythm
Eat bananas, beans, and leafy vegetables — rich in heart-healthy potassium

see_doctor_if: Palpitations with chest pain, shortness of breath, or fainting — seek care urgently
Palpitations that last more than 30 minutes
Regular palpitations occurring daily
Palpitations in someone with known heart disease
Palpitations with extreme dizziness or near-fainting
palpitations.local_context: Palpitations from anaemia are particularly common in Uganda among women of reproductive age and people with heavy malaria burden. A simple blood count can identify this. Anaemia causes the heart to work harder to deliver oxygen, leading to pounding awareness of heartbeat.
home_remedies: Cold water face splash — stimulates the vagus nerve
Coughing forcefully — can reset heart rhythm during an episode
Potassium-rich foods — bananas, avocado, beans, spinach
Magnesium-rich foods — pumpkin seeds, dark leafy greens, whole grains

anaemia.name: Anaemia
anaemia.description: A condition where the blood does not carry enough oxygen — either due to too few red blood cells or too little haemoglobin. Causes fatigue, pallor, breathlessness, and dizziness. Extremely common in Uganda, especially in women and children.
anaemia.body_mechanism: Red blood cells carry oxygen from your lungs to every cell in your body. When haemoglobin levels are low — due to iron deficiency, malaria, blood loss, or nutritional deficiency — your tissues receive less oxygen. Your heart compensates by beating faster (causing palpitations). Your brain receives less oxygen (causing dizziness and difficulty concentrating). Your muscles lack energy (causing fatigue).

immediate: Rest and avoid strenuous activity — your blood is delivering less oxygen than normal
Eat iron-rich foods today — beans, beef, dark leafy greens, liver, pumpkin seeds
Drink orange juice or eat vitamin C with iron-rich foods — vitamin C doubles iron absorption
Do not drink tea or coffee with meals — tannins block iron absorption
See a doctor or nurse for a blood test — you need to know your haemoglobin level
short_term: Take iron supplements as prescribed — ferrous sulphate is the most common
Continue eating iron-rich foods at every meal
Treat the underlying cause — malaria anaemia needs anti-malarials, hookworm needs deworming
Take iron supplements with vitamin C (orange juice) and away from tea and coffee
Iron supplements can cause dark stools and constipation — this is normal
long_term: Eat iron-rich foods regularly — beans, lentils, liver, dark leafy greens, fortified foods
Deworm regularly — intestinal worms consume nutrients and cause blood loss
For women — manage heavy menstrual periods which cause iron loss
Prevent and treat malaria promptly — malaria destroys red blood cells
Follow-up blood test after 3 months of treatment to confirm improvement

see_doctor_if: Severe pallor with extreme weakness — may need blood transfusion
Breathlessness at rest or during minimal activity
Chest pain or very fast heartbeat
Anaemia in a pregnant woman — needs urgent treatment
Anaemia not improving after 3 months of iron supplements
anaemia.local_context: Anaemia affects up to 40% of women and 60% of children under 5 in Uganda. The main causes are iron deficiency, malaria, hookworm, and nutritional deficiency. It is one of the most treatable conditions — simple iron supplements and dietary changes make a dramatic difference.
home_remedies: Liver — richest food source of haem iron, available and affordable in Uganda
Beans and lentils — excellent non-haem iron, always combine with vitamin C
Dark green vegetables — spinach, kale, sukuma wiki — eaten with tomato increases iron absorption
Moringa leaves — exceptionally iron-rich, grow widely in Uganda

diabetes_symptoms.name: Possible Diabetes (Type 2)
diabetes_symptoms.description: Type 2 diabetes develops when the body cannot use insulin effectively, causing blood sugar to remain high. Often symptomless early on, but classic symptoms include excessive thirst, frequent urination, and unexplained fatigue. Increasingly common in urban Uganda.
diabetes_symptoms.body_mechanism: Insulin acts as a key that opens cells to receive glucose from the blood. When cells become resistant to insulin, glucose builds up in the blood instead of entering cells. High blood glucose damages blood vessels and nerves over time. The kidneys try to flush excess glucose by producing more urine — which draws water with it, causing thirst and dehydration. Cells starved of glucose despite high blood sugar causes the fatigue.

immediate: See a doctor or clinic for a blood glucose test — this is the only way to confirm
Stop adding sugar to food and drinks immediately
Stop drinking sodas, juices, and sugary drinks completely
Drink water instead — plain water, not flavoured or sweetened
Write down your symptoms and any family history of diabetes to tell the doctor
short_term: Get a fasting blood glucose test and HbA1c — standard diagnostic tests
Begin reducing refined carbohydrates — white bread, white rice, posho, sweet potatoes
Increase vegetables, beans, and wholegrains
Begin daily walking — 30 minutes daily reduces blood sugar significantly
Lose weight if overweight — 5-10% weight loss dramatically improves blood sugar control
long_term: Take prescribed diabetes medication consistently — do not stop without doctor advice
Monitor blood glucose regularly if possible
Attend diabetes clinic follow-ups every 3-6 months
Protect your feet — diabetes damages foot nerves and circulation
Check eyes annually — diabetes damages the retina silently

see_doctor_if: Any of these symptoms — always needs a blood test to rule in or out
Extreme thirst and very frequent urination — classic diabetes symptoms
Unexplained weight loss despite eating normally
Wounds that do not heal normally
Known diabetic with blood sugar readings above 15mmol/L
diabetes_symptoms.local_context: Type 2 diabetes is rapidly increasing in Uganda, particularly in urban areas, driven by changes in diet and physical activity. Many people have it for years without knowing. A simple blood test at any clinic can diagnose it. Early detection and treatment prevents serious complications.
home_remedies: Bitter leaf (Vernonia amygdalina) — traditional remedy with evidence of mild blood sugar lowering
Moringa leaf powder in food — some evidence for mild glucose reduction
Daily walking — one of the most effective and evidence-based treatments for type 2 diabetes
Reducing refined carbohydrates and increasing vegetables, beans, and wholegrains

skin_rash.name: Skin Rash Assessment
skin_rash.description: A change in skin appearance — redness, bumps, blisters, or scaling. Rashes have many causes including allergic reactions, infections (fungal, bacterial, viral), heat, and systemic conditions. Most are harmless and self-limiting.
skin_rash.body_mechanism: The skin reacts to threats — internal or external — by releasing histamine and other inflammatory chemicals. This dilates blood vessels (causing redness), allows fluid to leak into tissue (causing swelling), and stimulates nerve endings (causing itch). The pattern, distribution, and characteristics of the rash help identify the cause.

immediate: Identify and remove any new soaps, detergents, creams, or medications that may be the cause
Do not scratch — scratching breaks the skin, increasing infection risk
Apply calamine lotion or 1% hydrocortisone cream if available — reduces itch and inflammation
Keep the affected area clean and dry
Antihistamine tablet (like chlorpheniramine) reduces allergic rash itching significantly
short_term: Wear loose, breathable cotton clothing over the rash
Avoid heat and sweating which worsen most rashes
If fungal rash suspected — keep area dry, apply antifungal cream
Photograph the rash to show a doctor — rashes change and a photo helps diagnosis
See a doctor if rash is spreading, blistering, or not improving
long_term: Identify your allergic triggers — new products, foods, environments
Use fragrance-free soaps and detergents if sensitive skin
For recurrent fungal infections — keep skin dry, wear breathable fabrics
Manage underlying conditions — eczema, psoriasis need ongoing care

see_doctor_if: Rash with fever — some serious infections start with rash and fever
Rash spreading rapidly or covering large areas of the body
Blistering rash — particularly shingles or severe allergic reaction
Rash on the face, in the mouth, or affecting the eyes
Any rash with difficulty breathing — anaphylaxis, seek emergency help immediately
skin_rash.local_context: Fungal skin infections are very common in Uganda due to heat and humidity. Heat rash is also common. Scabies — a mite infestation causing intense itch — is common in crowded living conditions. Measles rash starts on the face and spreads downward with high fever.
home_remedies: Aloe vera gel — soothes and cools inflamed skin
Shea butter — moisturises and protects dry, irritated skin
Coconut oil — antifungal properties, helpful for fungal rashes
Oat bath — pour oat flour into warm bathwater, soothes eczema and allergic rash

malnutrition.name: Malnutrition / Nutritional Deficiency
malnutrition.description: A state where the body lacks essential nutrients — vitamins, minerals, proteins, or calories — needed for normal function. Common causes include inadequate diet, malabsorption, or chronic illness. Widespread in Uganda, especially in children.
malnutrition.body_mechanism: Every body function depends on nutrients. Protein deficiency impairs immune function and tissue repair. Iron deficiency reduces oxygen delivery. Vitamin A deficiency impairs vision and immunity. B-vitamin deficiency affects the nervous system and energy production. Calcium deficiency weakens bones. Without adequate nutrients, every system in the body functions below capacity.

immediate: Eat a meal with protein, carbohydrates, and vegetables today — balance matters
Include beans, eggs, or meat — protein is the most commonly deficient nutrient
Eat dark green vegetables daily — they contain iron, folate, and vitamins A and C
Drink clean water — dehydration mimics and worsens malnutrition symptoms
Severe malnutrition in a child — go to hospital or health centre today
short_term: See a nutritionist or health worker for a proper assessment
Take a multivitamin if diet is very limited
Increase food variety — no single food provides everything needed
Treat underlying causes — intestinal parasites, malaria, and TB all cause malnutrition
For children — use therapeutic foods (RUTF) if prescribed
long_term: Diversify diet to include all food groups daily
Grow a kitchen garden — even a small one improves nutritional status significantly
Deworm every 6 months — worms steal nutrients
Breastfeed exclusively for 6 months — provides ideal nutrition for infants
Access community nutrition programmes at health centres

see_doctor_if: Child not growing normally or losing weight
Swelling of legs and feet (oedema) with malnutrition — serious
Hair loss, skin changes, and extreme fatigue together
Night blindness — inability to see in dim light — vitamin A deficiency
Severe weakness preventing normal daily activities
malnutrition.local_context: Malnutrition remains common in Uganda, especially in children under 5 in rural areas and urban slums. However, even families with food security can have nutritional deficiency if the diet lacks variety. The main deficiencies in Uganda are iron, vitamin A, and zinc.
home_remedies: Moringa — one of the most nutritious plants available in Uganda, rich in iron, calcium, and vitamins
Orange-fleshed sweet potatoes — rich in vitamin A, widely available and affordable
Groundnuts (peanuts) — high protein, healthy fats, zinc, and B vitamins
Beans and lentils at every meal — affordable, complete protein when combined with grains

dengue.name: Dengue Fever
dengue.description: A mosquito-borne viral disease causing sudden high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, and intense body aches — sometimes called 'breakbone fever'. Increasingly reported in Uganda.
dengue.body_mechanism: The dengue virus infects white blood cells and triggers a massive immune response. This causes the characteristic high fever and intense pain. Critically, it reduces platelets — the blood cells that control clotting — which is why severe dengue can cause bleeding. The virus is spread by Aedes mosquitoes, which bite during the day — unlike malaria mosquitoes which bite at night.

immediate: Go to a clinic for a dengue blood test — dengue NS1 antigen test or CBC
Take ONLY paracetamol for fever — NEVER aspirin or ibuprofen — they dangerously increase bleeding risk
Drink large amounts of water and ORS — dengue causes rapid dehydration
Rest completely — this is non-negotiable with dengue
Watch for warning signs that mean you need hospital care urgently
short_term: Complete bed rest for the full fever period — usually 5-7 days
Continue drinking large amounts of fluid — coconut water, ORS, plain water
Monitor for bleeding — gums, nose, bruising, blood in urine or stool
Take paracetamol only every 6 hours for fever and pain
Return to hospital immediately if any warning signs appear
long_term: Use mosquito repellent daily — Aedes mosquitoes bite during daytime hours
Wear long sleeves during the day in dengue-affected areas
Eliminate standing water — Aedes breeds in small containers, flower pots, tyres
Window screens and mosquito nets reduce exposure
Second dengue infection can be more severe — take extra precautions if previously infected

see_doctor_if: Severe abdominal pain that does not stop
Persistent vomiting — cannot keep fluids down
Bleeding from gums, nose, or blood in urine/stool
Extreme fatigue or restlessness
Rapid breathing or difficulty breathing
All suspected dengue — needs blood test to confirm
dengue.local_context: Dengue is emerging in Uganda and East Africa, particularly in urban areas. It is often mistaken for malaria — the key difference is dengue has severe pain behind the eyes and intense bone pain, and is spread by day-biting mosquitoes. If a malaria test is negative but fever persists, test for dengue.
home_remedies: Papaya leaf juice — traditional remedy with evidence for raising platelet count
Coconut water — excellent electrolyte replacement
Paracetamol only — aspirin and ibuprofen are dangerous with dengue
Complete rest — absolutely essential

tb.name: Tuberculosis (TB)
tb.description: A bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, primarily affecting the lungs. One of the leading infectious disease killers in Uganda. Causes persistent cough, night sweats, weight loss, and fever. Curable with a full course of antibiotics.
tb.body_mechanism: TB bacteria are inhaled and settle in the lungs where the immune system walls them off in granulomas — small nodules of immune cells. In people with weakened immunity (HIV, malnutrition, stress), the bacteria break out and destroy lung tissue, causing the characteristic cavities and cough. The cough produces droplets that spread the disease to others.

immediate: Go to the nearest health centre or hospital for TB testing — sputum test and chest X-ray
Cover your mouth when coughing — TB spreads through the air to people around you
Separate your eating and sleeping space from family members while being tested
Do not start any antibiotics without a proper diagnosis — TB needs specific drugs
Tell the healthcare worker about all your symptoms including weight loss and night sweats
short_term: Start TB treatment immediately if diagnosed — the standard DOTS regimen is 6 months
Take EVERY dose of medication as prescribed — never skip even when feeling better
Attend all follow-up appointments — sputum tests confirm the treatment is working
Eat nutritious food — TB causes severe nutritional depletion
HIV test is recommended for all TB patients — HIV and TB together need combined treatment
long_term: Complete the FULL 6-month treatment course — stopping early causes drug-resistant TB
Ensure good ventilation in your home — open windows and doors
Regular nutritious meals restore immune function
Family members and close contacts should be screened
HIV treatment if co-infected dramatically improves TB treatment outcomes

see_doctor_if: Cough lasting more than 2-3 weeks — this is the most important warning sign
Coughing up blood — go urgently
Unexplained weight loss of more than 3kg
Drenching night sweats for more than a week
Close contact with a known TB patient
tb.local_context: Uganda has one of the highest TB burdens in Africa. TB is curable and treatment is FREE at all government health facilities. The biggest risk is not completing treatment — this creates drug-resistant TB which is much harder to treat. HIV-positive people are 20x more likely to develop TB.
home_remedies: Nutritious food — liver, eggs, beans, dark leafy greens — rebuilds the immune system
Fresh air and sunlight — UV light kills TB bacteria
Moringa — high nutrition density supports immune recovery
Rest — adequate sleep is essential during TB treatment

pneumonia.name: Pneumonia
pneumonia.description: A serious infection of the lungs causing the air sacs to fill with fluid or pus. Causes fever, productive cough, chest pain, and difficulty breathing. Can be life-threatening especially in children, elderly, and people with HIV.
pneumonia.body_mechanism: Bacteria, viruses, or fungi infect the tiny air sacs (alveoli) in the lungs. The immune response fills these sacs with inflammatory fluid — pus and mucus — instead of air. This reduces the amount of oxygen that can enter the blood. The body compensates by breathing faster. Severe pneumonia means so many alveoli are filled that oxygen levels fall dangerously.

immediate: Go to hospital now — pneumonia can progress very fast
Sit upright — do not lie flat, it worsens breathing
Take prescribed antibiotics exactly as directed — start immediately
Stay hydrated — fever and rapid breathing cause fast fluid loss
Monitor breathing rate — if breathing very fast or struggling, go to hospital urgently
short_term: Complete the full antibiotic course — usually 5-10 days
Rest completely for at least 1 week
Fever and cough may take 1-2 weeks to resolve even with treatment
Eat nutritious food to support immune recovery
Follow-up chest X-ray at 4-6 weeks to confirm clearance
long_term: Stop smoking completely — smoking is the biggest single risk factor
Treat underlying conditions — HIV, diabetes, and malnutrition all increase pneumonia risk
Get children vaccinated — pneumococcal vaccine prevents bacterial pneumonia
Avoid indoor smoke — cook in ventilated spaces
Seek care early for chest infections — early treatment prevents pneumonia

see_doctor_if: Any suspected pneumonia — always needs proper assessment and antibiotics
Breathing rate above 30 breaths per minute
Blue or grey lips or fingernails
Confusion or inability to stay awake
Chest pain that worsens with every breath
pneumonia.local_context: Pneumonia is the leading killer of children under 5 in Uganda. Adults with HIV are at very high risk. Early treatment with antibiotics is highly effective — the danger is delayed treatment. Any child with fast breathing and fever should be taken to hospital immediately.
home_remedies: Steam inhalation — loosens mucus and eases breathing
Propped up sleeping — use pillows to keep upper body elevated
Warm ginger and honey tea — soothes airways and provides energy
High fluid intake — thins mucus for easier expectoration

cholera.name: Cholera / Severe Diarrhoea
cholera.description: An acute diarrhoeal illness caused by Vibrio cholerae bacteria from contaminated water or food. Causes sudden, profuse watery diarrhoea and vomiting leading to rapid, life-threatening dehydration.
cholera.body_mechanism: The cholera toxin forces intestinal cells to pump chloride ions into the gut — water follows by osmosis. This creates the characteristic 'rice-water' diarrhoea — massive volumes of watery stool containing no blood. A person can lose 10-20 litres of fluid in a day. The resulting dehydration causes electrolyte imbalance, muscle cramps, low blood pressure, and if untreated, death within hours.

immediate: Start oral rehydration immediately — 1 litre clean water + 6 teaspoons sugar + 1/2 teaspoon salt
Drink the ORS solution constantly — small sips every few minutes
Go to hospital or health centre today — cholera needs IV fluids in severe cases
Do not use anti-diarrhoea tablets — they slow expulsion of the bacteria
Isolate contaminated items — cholera spreads very easily
short_term: IV fluids at hospital if unable to keep ORS down
Antibiotics as prescribed reduce the duration significantly
Continue ORS until diarrhoea completely stops
Boil all water for drinking, cooking, and washing dishes
Bleach any contaminated surfaces and clothing
long_term: Only drink boiled or treated water
Wash hands with soap before all food contact and after toilet
Cook food thoroughly and eat immediately — do not store cooked food
Report cholera cases to health authorities — it is a notifiable disease
Community water treatment and sanitation are the long-term solution

see_doctor_if: All suspected cholera — go immediately
Cannot keep any fluids down
Signs of severe dehydration — sunken eyes, dry mouth, no urination, extreme weakness
Muscle cramps
Multiple cases in the same household or community
cholera.local_context: Cholera outbreaks occur regularly in Uganda, especially in displacement camps, flood-affected areas, and around Lake Victoria. It can kill within hours if untreated. ORS (Oral Rehydration Salts) sachets are free at health centres — they save lives.
home_remedies: Homemade ORS is life-saving — 1L water + 6 teaspoons sugar + 0.5 teaspoon salt
Coconut water — good electrolyte replacement if ORS unavailable
Boiled water — absolutely essential
Zinc supplements — proven to reduce diarrhoea severity and duration

hiv_symptoms.name: HIV / AIDS Symptoms
hiv_symptoms.description: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) attacks the immune system. Primary infection causes a flu-like illness. Untreated HIV progresses to AIDS, causing susceptibility to other infections. With antiretroviral therapy (ART), people with HIV can live full, healthy lives.
hiv_symptoms.body_mechanism: HIV specifically infects and destroys CD4 T-cells — the immune system's command cells. As CD4 count falls, the body loses its ability to fight infections and cancers that a healthy immune system would control. The flu-like primary infection (acute HIV) occurs 2-6 weeks after infection as the virus replicates rapidly. Years later, with very low CD4 counts, opportunistic infections develop.

immediate: Get an HIV test — free and confidential at all Uganda health facilities and VCT centres
Testing is the only way to know your status — symptoms alone cannot diagnose HIV
If you have had a high-risk exposure in the last 72 hours — PEP (post-exposure prophylaxis) can prevent HIV — go to hospital immediately
Do not share needles, razors, or any blood-contact items
Use condoms consistently to prevent transmission
short_term: If test is positive — start antiretroviral therapy (ART) as soon as possible
ART is free at all government health facilities in Uganda
Enroll in HIV care at your nearest health facility
Screen for TB — the two conditions occur together very commonly
Eat nutritious food to support immune function
long_term: Take ART every single day — adherence is the most important factor in outcomes
Regular CD4 count and viral load monitoring
Prevent opportunistic infections with prophylactic medications
Maintain confidentiality of your status — discrimination is illegal
Support groups significantly improve adherence and wellbeing

see_doctor_if: Any suspected HIV exposure — test as soon as possible
Persistent fever, weight loss, and night sweats together
Recurring infections that do not resolve normally
Any opportunistic infection symptoms — PCP pneumonia, cryptococcal meningitis, toxoplasmosis
Within 72 hours of possible exposure — PEP can prevent infection
hiv_symptoms.local_context: Uganda has made enormous progress in HIV treatment — over 1.4 million Ugandans are on ART and living healthy lives. HIV testing is free and confidential. Treatment is free. Stigma remains a major barrier but is reducing. Knowing your status and starting treatment early is life-saving.
home_remedies: Nutritious, varied diet is essential — malnutrition worsens HIV progression significantly
Regular moderate exercise improves immune function and mental health
Avoid alcohol — it reduces ART adherence and accelerates liver damage
Moringa, beans, eggs, and dark leafy greens support immune nutrition

kidney_stones.name: Kidney Stones
kidney_stones.description: Hard deposits of minerals and salts that form inside the kidneys and cause intense pain as they move through the urinary tract. The pain is often described as one of the worst pains a person can experience.
kidney_stones.body_mechanism: When urine becomes highly concentrated — due to dehydration or dietary factors — minerals crystallise and clump together. These crystals grow into stones ranging from a grain of sand to a marble. When a stone moves from the kidney into the ureter (the tube to the bladder), it causes excruciating colicky pain that comes in waves as the ureter contracts trying to push the stone through.

immediate: Drink 2-3 large glasses of water immediately — increased urine flow helps pass the stone
Take ibuprofen or diclofenac for pain — they relax the ureter and reduce spasms
Apply heat to your flank — warm water bottle on the painful side
Go to hospital if pain is unbearable or you have fever — fever suggests infection
Strain your urine to catch the stone if possible — helps confirm diagnosis
short_term: Drink at least 3 litres of water daily until stone passes
Most small stones (under 5mm) pass on their own within 4 weeks
Pain medication as prescribed for the duration
Avoid foods high in oxalate if calcium oxalate stones — chocolate, spinach, nuts
Follow up with a doctor — imaging may be needed for large stones
long_term: Drink 2-3 litres of water every single day — the most effective prevention
Reduce salt intake — high salt increases calcium in urine
Reduce animal protein — it increases uric acid
Eat calcium-rich foods with meals — helps bind dietary oxalate
If recurrent stones — specialist referral for metabolic evaluation

see_doctor_if: Fever with kidney stone pain — indicates infection, which is an emergency
Unable to urinate at all
Pain not controlled with over-the-counter medication
Vomiting preventing fluid intake and medication
Stone larger than 6mm — likely needs medical intervention
kidney_stones.local_context: Kidney stones are increasing in Uganda with urbanisation and dietary changes. Dehydration in Uganda's heat is the biggest risk factor. Drinking adequate water every day is the single most effective prevention.
home_remedies: Large amounts of water — most important treatment
Lemon juice in water — citrate inhibits stone formation
Heat on the flank for pain relief
Basil juice — traditional remedy with some evidence for reducing uric acid

appendicitis.name: Appendicitis
appendicitis.description: Inflammation of the appendix — a small pouch attached to the large intestine. Causes severe abdominal pain that starts around the navel and moves to the lower right. A surgical emergency — a ruptured appendix is life-threatening.
appendicitis.body_mechanism: The appendix becomes blocked — by stool, mucus, or infection — causing bacteria to multiply inside. The resulting infection causes inflammation, swelling, and increased pressure. If untreated, the appendix can rupture within 24-72 hours, spilling bacteria into the abdomen and causing life-threatening peritonitis.

immediate: Go to hospital immediately — appendicitis is a surgical emergency
Do not eat or drink anything — you may need surgery
Do not take laxatives or apply heat to the abdomen
Take nothing by mouth until seen by a doctor
Tell the doctor exactly where the pain started and where it is now
short_term: Surgery (appendectomy) is the definitive treatment
Antibiotics are given before and after surgery
Recovery from laparoscopic surgery is typically 1-2 weeks
Avoid strenuous activity for 4-6 weeks after surgery
Follow all post-operative instructions precisely
long_term: No long-term dietary changes needed after appendectomy
Full recovery with no lasting impact on digestive function
Watch for signs of infection at the incision site after surgery
Return to normal activities gradually as advised by surgeon

see_doctor_if: Pain that moves from the navel to lower right abdomen — classic appendicitis
Lower right abdominal pain with fever and vomiting
Abdomen that is rigid or very tender to touch
Any severe abdominal pain that is worsening — go immediately
Pain that briefly improves then becomes much worse — may indicate rupture
appendicitis.local_context: Appendicitis can occur at any age and is a true surgical emergency. In Uganda, delayed presentation is common, increasing the risk of rupture. Any lower right abdominal pain with fever in a young person must be taken seriously and assessed urgently.
home_remedies: There are NO home remedies for appendicitis — surgery is the only treatment
Do not apply heat, take laxatives, or try to wait it out
Every hour of delay increases the risk of rupture

stroke_symptoms.name: Stroke Warning Signs
stroke_symptoms.description: A stroke occurs when blood supply to part of the brain is cut off — either by a clot (ischaemic) or bleeding (haemorrhagic). Every minute without treatment causes irreversible brain damage. Remember FAST: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call for help.
stroke_symptoms.body_mechanism: Brain cells need a constant supply of oxygen from blood. When a blood vessel is blocked or bursts, the brain cells in that area begin dying within minutes. Different areas of the brain control different functions — which symptoms appear depends on which area is affected. TIME IS THE MOST CRITICAL FACTOR: for every minute of stroke, 1.9 million brain cells die.

immediate: Call for help IMMEDIATELY — do not wait
Get to the nearest hospital with a doctor NOW — time is brain
Note the exact time symptoms started — doctors need this for treatment decisions
Do not give food, water, or medication by mouth — swallowing may be impaired
Keep the person calm and lying down with head slightly elevated
short_term: Clot-busting medication (thrombolysis) can be given within 4.5 hours of symptoms — this is why speed matters
Aspirin is given immediately for ischaemic stroke — do NOT give for suspected brain bleed
Blood pressure control and monitoring in hospital
Rehabilitation — physiotherapy, speech therapy — begins as early as possible
Prevent complications — aspiration, pressure sores, blood clots in legs
long_term: Rehabilitation is intensive and long — motor and speech recovery can continue for years
Control all stroke risk factors — blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, cholesterol
Anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation to prevent recurrent strokes
Lifestyle changes — diet, exercise, no smoking are essential
Family education on stroke signs and response

see_doctor_if: ANY of the FAST signs — Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty — go IMMEDIATELY
Sudden worst-ever headache with no warning
Sudden vision loss in one or both eyes
Sudden loss of balance or coordination
Sudden confusion or difficulty understanding — go immediately
stroke_symptoms.local_context: Stroke is increasing in Uganda as hypertension becomes more common. The window for effective treatment is short — 4.5 hours from symptom onset for the most powerful treatments. Knowing FAST and acting immediately saves lives and reduces disability. Mulago and other major hospitals have stroke units.
home_remedies: There are NO home remedies for stroke — hospital is the ONLY option
Every minute of delay causes permanent brain damage
FAST — Face, Arms, Speech, Time — memorise and act immediately

scabies.name: Scabies
scabies.description: A highly contagious skin infestation caused by tiny mites (Sarcoptes scabiei) that burrow into the skin. Causes intense itching — especially at night — and a pimple-like rash. Spreads easily through close skin contact.
