scabies.body_mechanism: The female mite burrows into the outer skin layer and lays eggs. After 3-4 days the eggs hatch, and the cycle repeats. The itching is caused by the body's allergic reaction to the mites, their eggs, and their waste. The itch is worse at night because body temperature rises in warm bedding, making the mites more active.

immediate: Apply permethrin 5% cream (from pharmacy) to ALL skin from neck to toes — leave for 8-14 hours then wash off
Treat all household members and close contacts simultaneously — even if they have no symptoms
Take an antihistamine tablet to help with itching
Do not scratch — it spreads the mites and causes skin infections
Wash all bedding, clothing, and towels in hot water today
short_term: Repeat treatment after 1 week — kills newly hatched mites
Itching may continue for 2-4 weeks after treatment even when mites are gone — this is normal
Continue antihistamines for itch relief as needed
All clothing and bedding used in the 3 days before treatment must be washed in hot water
Items that cannot be washed — seal in a plastic bag for 1 week
long_term: Avoid close skin contact with infected people until treated
Change bedding regularly and wash in hot water
Early treatment prevents spreading to family and community
Treat the whole household — individual treatment fails if others are not treated

see_doctor_if: Rash becomes infected — pus, increased redness, or spreading cellulitis
Permethrin not available — doctor can prescribe alternatives including oral ivermectin
Infants under 2 months — need different treatment
Persistent severe infestation despite 2 rounds of treatment
Crusted (Norwegian) scabies — thick crusting skin — highly contagious and needs specialist treatment
scabies.local_context: Scabies is extremely common in Uganda, especially in schools, children's homes, and crowded housing. The key sign is intense itch that is worse at night, especially between fingers, wrists, and armpits. Permethrin cream is available at pharmacies. Treating the whole family at once is essential.
home_remedies: Neem oil — traditional antiparasitic with evidence against scabies mites
Sulphur ointment — traditional remedy widely used in Uganda, effective but smells strongly
Tea tree oil diluted in carrier oil — antiparasitic properties
Antihistamine tablets — reduces itch while waiting for treatment to work

peptic_ulcer.name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
peptic_ulcer.description: An open sore in the lining of the stomach or duodenum (first part of the small intestine). Caused mainly by H. pylori bacteria or regular NSAID use. Causes a burning or gnawing pain in the upper abdomen, often related to meals.
peptic_ulcer.body_mechanism: The stomach lining is protected by a thick mucus barrier. H. pylori bacteria weaken this barrier by releasing enzymes that break down the protective mucus. NSAIDs (ibuprofen, aspirin, diclofenac) directly inhibit the enzymes that produce protective prostaglandins. With the protection gone, stomach acid burns directly into the underlying tissue, creating an ulcer — an open wound in the stomach or duodenum.

immediate: Stop ibuprofen, aspirin, and diclofenac immediately — they directly damage the stomach lining
Take an antacid (aluminium hydroxide, magnesium hydroxide) for immediate relief
Eat something — even crackers or plain rice — the pain is often worse on an empty stomach
Avoid coffee, alcohol, spicy food, and acidic foods — all irritate the ulcer
See a doctor for proper diagnosis and treatment — H. pylori needs specific antibiotics
short_term: Take proton pump inhibitors (omeprazole, pantoprazole) as prescribed — very effective
H. pylori eradication: triple therapy — 2 antibiotics + PPI for 14 days
Eat smaller meals more frequently — reduces acid exposure
Avoid lying down for 2 hours after eating
Avoid NSAIDs permanently if possible — use paracetamol instead for pain
long_term: Complete the full H. pylori eradication course — partial treatment causes resistance
Maintain regular meal times — empty stomach worsens ulcer pain
Reduce stress — stress increases acid production
Avoid NSAIDs long-term — if essential, always take with omeprazole
Follow-up endoscopy recommended for gastric ulcers to confirm healing

see_doctor_if: Vomiting blood or material like coffee grounds
Black, tarry stools — indicates stomach bleeding
Severe pain that is constant rather than coming in waves
Unexplained weight loss with ulcer symptoms
Symptoms not improving after 2 weeks of antacid treatment
peptic_ulcer.local_context: Peptic ulcers are very common in Uganda. H. pylori infects up to 70% of Ugandans — it spreads through contaminated water and food. The widespread use of ibuprofen for malaria-related body aches is a major contributing factor. Both causes are very treatable with the right medication.
home_remedies: Raw honey — has proven antibacterial activity against H. pylori
Cabbage juice — traditional remedy with some evidence for ulcer healing
Banana — coating effect on the stomach lining, reduces irritation
Aloe vera juice — soothes inflamed stomach lining

meningitis.name: Meningitis
meningitis.description: Inflammation of the meninges — the protective membranes covering the brain and spinal cord. Caused by bacterial or viral infection. Bacterial meningitis is a medical emergency that can cause death or disability within hours.
meningitis.body_mechanism: Bacteria or viruses enter the bloodstream and cross into the cerebrospinal fluid surrounding the brain and spinal cord. The resulting infection and inflammation cause the classic triad of symptoms: severe headache (from increased pressure), stiff neck (from inflammation irritating the spinal meninges), and fever (from the immune response). The rapidly increasing pressure inside the skull can be fatal without immediate treatment.

immediate: Go to hospital IMMEDIATELY — bacterial meningitis can kill within hours
Do not wait — this is a true medical emergency
Tell the doctor about ALL symptoms including the exact sequence they appeared
Antibiotics must be started urgently — every hour of delay worsens outcomes
Call for help to transport you — do not attempt to drive yourself
short_term: High-dose IV antibiotics are the life-saving treatment
IV dexamethasone reduces brain swelling and neurological complications
Intensive monitoring in hospital
Close contacts may need prophylactic antibiotics
Recovery can take weeks to months
long_term: Some neurological effects may be permanent — hearing loss, memory problems
Rehabilitation as needed — hearing aids, cognitive therapy
Vaccination prevents meningococcal and pneumococcal meningitis
Family and close contacts should be monitored for symptoms in the following 10 days

see_doctor_if: Severe headache + stiff neck + fever together — go immediately
Inability to bend chin to chest — classic meningism sign
A rash that does not blanch when pressed — meningococcal septicaemia
Confusion, seizures, or altered consciousness — go immediately
Any combination of these symptoms in a child — do not wait
meningitis.local_context: Bacterial meningitis is a serious cause of death and disability in Uganda, particularly in children. Cryptococcal meningitis is common in HIV-positive patients. The non-blanching rash — press a glass against it — is specific to meningococcal disease and requires immediate hospital care.
home_remedies: There are NO home remedies for meningitis — hospital is the ONLY option
Any delay in reaching hospital increases the risk of death or permanent brain damage
Go immediately — do not try to manage this at home

heart_failure.name: Heart Failure Symptoms
heart_failure.description: A condition where the heart cannot pump blood efficiently enough to meet the body's needs. Causes breathlessness, leg swelling, fatigue, and fluid build-up. Requires medical management — very manageable with proper treatment.
heart_failure.body_mechanism: When the heart pumps weakly, fluid backs up — in the lungs (causing breathlessness when lying flat), and in the legs and abdomen (causing swelling). The kidneys try to compensate by retaining fluid, which makes the problem worse. The body redirects blood from non-essential organs to vital ones, causing fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance.

immediate: Sit upright — lying flat worsens fluid in the lungs and breathing difficulty
Do not exert yourself — rest immediately
If prescribed diuretics (frusemide) — take them as prescribed
Go to hospital if breathing difficulty is severe or suddenly worsening
Restrict fluid and salt intake today
short_term: See a doctor urgently for formal assessment and ECG
Diuretics remove excess fluid — take exactly as prescribed
ACE inhibitors or ARBs reduce the strain on the heart
Weigh yourself daily — rapid weight gain means fluid is accumulating
Restrict salt to less than 2g per day — salt causes fluid retention
long_term: Take all medications consistently — stopping causes rapid deterioration
Weigh daily — report 2kg gain in 2 days to your doctor
Salt restriction is essential and permanent
Regular gentle exercise as tolerated improves heart function over time
Treat the underlying cause — hypertension, rheumatic heart disease, anaemia

see_doctor_if: Sudden severe breathlessness — emergency
Breathlessness lying flat that forces you to sleep sitting up
Rapid weight gain of 2kg or more in 2 days
Increasing leg swelling
Confusion or extreme fatigue — signs of severely reduced cardiac output
heart_failure.local_context: Heart failure is increasingly common in Uganda, mainly from untreated hypertension, rheumatic heart disease from childhood streptococcal infections, and peripartum cardiomyopathy in women after delivery. Many cases are preventable with early blood pressure treatment.
home_remedies: Salt restriction — the most important dietary intervention
Elevate legs when sitting — reduces ankle swelling
Weigh daily at the same time — the most important monitoring tool
Avoid alcohol completely — it directly weakens heart muscle

eye_strain.name: Eye Strain / Digital Eye Fatigue
eye_strain.description: Tired, uncomfortable eyes caused by prolonged use of screens, reading, or poor lighting. Extremely common in the modern world. Causes headaches behind the eyes, blurred vision, and eye discomfort. Not dangerous — fully reversible.
eye_strain.body_mechanism: When focusing on close objects or screens for extended periods, the ciliary muscles inside your eyes contract continuously to maintain focus — they never relax. This sustained muscle tension causes fatigue just like any other muscle overuse. Screens also reduce your blink rate significantly (from 15 to 5 blinks per minute), causing dry, irritated eyes. Blue light from screens may also affect circadian rhythms.

immediate: Apply the 20-20-20 rule immediately — every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds
Blink consciously and frequently — long blinks, fully closing eyes
Reduce screen brightness to match the ambient light level
Rest your eyes completely — close them for 5-10 minutes
Apply a warm compress to closed eyelids — relaxes ciliary muscles
short_term: Adjust your screen position — arm's length away, top of screen at eye level
Increase font size — smaller text requires more effort
Use night mode or blue light filter, especially in evenings
Ensure good lighting — no screen glare, not working in the dark
Artificial tear drops for dry eye symptoms — available at pharmacies
long_term: Implement regular screen breaks — schedule them, not just when you remember
Get eyes tested — uncorrected refractive errors massively worsen eye strain
Reduce total screen time where possible
Optimise your workspace lighting — indirect lighting, no glare
Consider blue light blocking glasses if spending 6+ hours on screens daily

see_doctor_if: Eye pain that persists after rest
Significant vision changes that do not resolve
Double vision
Eye pain with redness — may be something more serious
Headaches every day that start behind the eyes
eye_strain.local_context: Rapidly increasing in Uganda with smartphone penetration and students using devices for study. Many Ugandans have uncorrected refractive errors (short or long sight) that go undetected, dramatically worsening eye strain. Free eye clinics are available at major hospitals.
home_remedies: Cucumber slices on closed eyes — soothes and cools tired eyes
Rose water eye drops — traditional soothing remedy
Warm compress of clean cloth — relaxes eye muscles
Eye exercises — look up, down, left, right, then rotate — relieves muscle tension

worms.name: Intestinal Worms / Helminthiasis
worms.description: Parasitic worm infections of the intestines — including roundworm, hookworm, tapeworm, and pinworm. Extremely common in Uganda. Causes abdominal discomfort, nutritional deficiency, and anaemia. Easily treated and prevented.
worms.body_mechanism: Different worms infect through different routes. Hookworm larvae in soil penetrate bare feet and travel to the intestine. Roundworm and tapeworm eggs are swallowed in contaminated food and water. In the intestine, worms consume nutrients directly from your gut — causing nutritional deficiency. Hookworm specifically causes iron deficiency anaemia by feeding on blood from the intestinal wall.

immediate: Take a single dose of mebendazole 500mg or albendazole 400mg — available at all pharmacies
Wash hands thoroughly with soap before every meal and after every toilet visit
Wash all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating
Do not walk barefoot on soil — hookworm enters through the skin of feet
Deworm all household members simultaneously
short_term: Repeat deworming dose after 2 weeks for pinworm — eggs remain viable
Wash bedsheets, nightwear, and underwear in hot water
Trim fingernails short — eggs collect under long nails
Increase iron-rich foods — beans, liver, dark leafy greens — to address anaemia from hookworm
Continue hygiene measures rigorously for 2 weeks
long_term: Deworm every 6 months as routine prevention — especially for children
Always wear shoes or sandals outdoors — prevents hookworm
Wash hands with soap religiously — before eating, after toilet
Cook meat thoroughly — prevents tapeworm from undercooked pork or beef
Drink only treated or boiled water

see_doctor_if: Visible worms in stool
Severe abdominal pain — could indicate worm obstruction
Significant weight loss with worm symptoms
Symptoms not improving after treatment
Child with visible worms and poor growth
worms.local_context: Intestinal worms are one of the most common health problems in Uganda, affecting up to 50% of children in rural areas. Deworming tablets (mebendazole) are free for children at schools and health centres. Routine deworming every 6 months combined with hygiene is the most effective strategy.
home_remedies: Papaya seeds — traditional antiparasitic, grind and eat 1 tablespoon with honey
Pumpkin seeds — contain cucurbitacin which paralyses worms
Garlic — raw garlic has antiparasitic properties against several worm species
Coconut — coconut flesh and oil have antiparasitic properties

period_pain.name: Painful Periods (Dysmenorrhoea)
period_pain.description: Painful menstrual cramps before or during a period. One of the most common gynaecological conditions — affecting up to 80% of women at some point. Primary dysmenorrhoea is cramps without underlying disease. Secondary dysmenorrhoea is caused by endometriosis or fibroids.
period_pain.body_mechanism: During menstruation, the uterus contracts to expel its lining. These contractions are triggered by prostaglandins — hormone-like chemicals. High prostaglandin levels cause stronger, more painful contractions that can temporarily reduce blood flow to the uterine muscle — causing the cramping pain. The same prostaglandins can cause nausea, diarrhoea, and headaches.

immediate: Take ibuprofen at the first sign of cramps — it blocks prostaglandins directly
Apply a warm compress or hot water bottle to your lower abdomen — significantly reduces cramp intensity
Lie on your side with knees drawn up — fetal position reduces uterine pressure
Light gentle stretching — yoga child's pose and hip circles can help
If ibuprofen is not available — paracetamol gives partial relief
short_term: Start ibuprofen 1-2 days before your period begins if cramps are predictable — prevents prostaglandin build-up
Regular exercise throughout the month reduces period pain significantly
Reduce caffeine and salt in the week before your period
Magnesium-rich foods — pumpkin seeds, dark chocolate, leafy greens — reduce cramp severity
Vitamin D and omega-3 supplements have good evidence for reducing period pain
long_term: If pain severely affects your daily life — see a doctor for investigation
Secondary causes (endometriosis, fibroids) need medical treatment
Hormonal contraception reduces period pain significantly for many women
Regular aerobic exercise reduces prostaglandin levels over time
Track your cycle — knowing when to start pain relief gives much better control

see_doctor_if: Pain so severe it prevents normal activities despite medication
Pain worsening each cycle over several months
Unusually heavy bleeding with pain
Pain that continues outside your period
Painful intercourse alongside period pain — possible endometriosis
period_pain.local_context: Period pain is often dismissed in Uganda as something women must endure. This is wrong — severe period pain is a medical condition that deserves treatment. Endometriosis is underdiagnosed across Africa. If your pain is severe, you deserve proper investigation and treatment.
home_remedies: Hot water bottle on lower abdomen — one of the most effective immediate remedies
Ginger tea — reduces prostaglandin levels similar to mild ibuprofen
Fennel seed tea — traditional remedy with evidence for reducing cramp intensity
Warm turmeric milk — anti-inflammatory properties help with cramping

heat_exhaustion.name: Heat Exhaustion / Heat Stroke
heat_exhaustion.description: A condition caused by overheating — either heat exhaustion (heavy sweating, weakness, fast pulse) or the more serious heat stroke (body temperature above 40°C, confusion, no sweating). Heat stroke is a medical emergency.
heat_exhaustion.body_mechanism: Your body normally cools itself through sweating. In extreme heat or with prolonged exertion, the cooling system can be overwhelmed. Heat exhaustion occurs when the body loses too much fluid and salt through sweating. Heat stroke occurs when the body's temperature regulation completely fails — body temperature rises to dangerous levels (above 40°C) causing proteins in cells to denature and organs to fail.

immediate: Move to the coolest available place immediately — shade, air conditioning, or fan
Remove excess clothing
Cool the body — cool (not icy) water on skin, especially neck, armpits, and groin
Drink cool water slowly — small sips if conscious
If confused, seizures, or no sweating despite heat — this is HEAT STROKE, call for emergency help now
short_term: Rest in a cool environment for at least several hours
Drink ORS solution — replaces both fluid and electrolytes lost in sweat
Do not return to heat exposure until fully recovered — at least 24 hours
Monitor temperature if possible — should return to below 38°C
Seek medical attention if any confusion or persistent symptoms
long_term: Acclimatise gradually to hot environments — your body needs 1-2 weeks
Drink 2-3 litres of water in hot weather even if not thirsty
Wear light, loose, light-coloured clothing outdoors
Schedule outdoor work for cooler parts of the day — early morning, evening
Recognise early warning signs — act before they progress to heat stroke

see_doctor_if: Confusion, seizures, or unconsciousness — heat stroke, go immediately
Body temperature above 40°C
No sweating despite extreme heat
Symptoms not improving after 30-60 minutes of cooling
Heat illness in elderly people, children under 5, or those with heart/kidney disease
heat_exhaustion.local_context: Heat exhaustion is common in Uganda during hot season, especially in people doing heavy outdoor work, athletes, and those travelling long distances in overcrowded vehicles without water. Heat stroke is a medical emergency — Uganda's heat combined with manual labour creates significant risk.
home_remedies: Move to shade and fan the person immediately
Pour cool water over the body — especially neck, armpits, groin
ORS solution or coconut water — replaces electrolytes
Wet cloths on forehead and neck — evaporative cooling

malaria_severe.name: Severe Malaria
malaria_severe.description: Life-threatening malaria with organ involvement — brain (cerebral malaria), kidneys, lungs, or severe anaemia. A medical emergency requiring immediate IV treatment in hospital.
malaria_severe.body_mechanism: When malaria parasites infect red blood cells in massive numbers, the infected cells become sticky and block small blood vessels in vital organs. In cerebral malaria, blocked brain vessels cause seizures and unconsciousness. Kidney blockage causes acute kidney failure. Massive destruction of red blood cells causes severe anaemia. Without IV artesunate within hours, death is likely.

immediate: Call for transport to hospital NOW — this is a life-threatening emergency
Do not attempt home treatment — IV artesunate must be given in hospital
Lay the person on their side if unconscious — recovery position
Keep them cool — fan and remove excess clothing
Note exactly when symptoms started and tell the doctor
short_term: IV artesunate is the gold-standard treatment — insist on it if available
IV fluids for dehydration and kidney support
Blood transfusion if severely anaemic
Intensive monitoring in hospital — oxygen, blood glucose, kidney function
long_term: Full recovery possible with prompt treatment
Cerebral malaria can cause neurological effects — monitor for seizures, behaviour changes
Prevent reinfection — sleep under nets every night
Children who survive cerebral malaria need school monitoring for learning difficulties

see_doctor_if: Any confusion or altered consciousness with fever — go immediately
Inability to walk or sit up with fever
Yellow eyes (jaundice) with fever
Coca-cola coloured urine with fever
Seizures with fever
malaria_severe.local_context: Severe malaria kills thousands of Ugandan children every year — most deaths occur because families wait too long before going to hospital. Any child with fever AND confusion, inability to walk, or seizures must reach hospital within the hour.
home_remedies: There are NO home remedies for severe malaria — hospital is the only option
Give nothing by mouth if unconscious
Transport to hospital is the only correct action

tonsillitis.name: Tonsillitis
tonsillitis.description: Inflammation of the tonsils — the two lymph nodes at the back of your throat. Causes severe sore throat, difficulty swallowing, fever, and swollen lymph nodes in the neck. Can be viral or bacterial.
tonsillitis.body_mechanism: The tonsils are your throat's first immune defence — they trap bacteria and viruses entering through the mouth. When overwhelmed by infection, they become inflamed and swollen. Bacterial tonsillitis (usually Streptococcus) causes more severe symptoms and requires antibiotics. Viral tonsillitis resolves on its own but causes similar discomfort.

immediate: Gargle warm salt water — half teaspoon salt in a glass of warm water — every 2 hours
Take paracetamol or ibuprofen for pain and fever
Drink warm fluids — tea with honey and lemon, warm soup, warm water
Rest your voice — talking increases throat irritation
Stay well hydrated — sore throat makes drinking uncomfortable but it is essential
short_term: See a doctor if symptoms are severe or persist beyond 3-4 days — may need antibiotics for strep
Complete antibiotic course if prescribed — stopping early causes recurrence
Eat soft foods — yoghurt, porridge, mashed food — while swallowing is painful
Cool drinks and ice can soothe the throat pain
Honey and lemon in warm water is highly effective for symptom relief
long_term: Recurrent tonsillitis (more than 4-5 times per year) may require tonsillectomy — discuss with doctor
Maintain good hand hygiene — tonsillitis spreads person-to-person
Avoid sharing cups and utensils during infection
Gargling with salt water regularly can reduce frequency of infections

see_doctor_if: Cannot open mouth fully — possible peritonsillar abscess (emergency)
Drooling because unable to swallow
Breathing difficulty
High fever not responding to paracetamol
Symptoms lasting more than 1 week without improvement
tonsillitis.local_context: Tonsillitis is very common in Uganda, especially in school-age children. Streptococcal tonsillitis that is not treated with antibiotics can lead to rheumatic fever — a serious complication causing permanent heart damage. Always complete antibiotic courses.
home_remedies: Honey and warm water — coating and antibacterial properties for throat
Turmeric and salt gargle — anti-inflammatory and antibacterial
Ginger tea with honey — reduces inflammation and soothes
Steam inhalation with eucalyptus — opens airways and reduces congestion

ear_infection.name: Ear Infection (Otitis Media)
ear_infection.description: Infection of the middle ear — the space behind the eardrum. Causes ear pain, reduced hearing, and sometimes discharge. Very common in children under 5. Usually bacterial, often following a cold.
ear_infection.body_mechanism: The middle ear connects to the back of the throat via the Eustachian tube. When this tube becomes blocked during a cold or upper respiratory infection, bacteria can multiply in the trapped fluid in the middle ear. The resulting infection causes pressure and inflammation — causing the characteristic ear pain. In children, the Eustachian tube is shorter and more horizontal, making infections easier.

immediate: Paracetamol or ibuprofen for pain — ear infection pain can be very severe
Warm (not hot) compress against the ear — relieves pain significantly
Keep ear dry — no swimming or submerging
Prop the head up slightly for sleep — reduces pressure in the middle ear
Do not insert anything into the ear canal — cotton buds, sticks — worsens infection
short_term: See a doctor — most bacterial ear infections need antibiotics
Amoxicillin is the standard first-line antibiotic
Most ear infections clear within 2-3 days of antibiotics
Persistent discharge from the ear means the eardrum has perforated — needs medical review
Children with recurrent ear infections need hearing assessment
long_term: Treat colds promptly — ear infections often follow colds
Avoid cigarette smoke exposure — increases risk significantly in children
Breastfeeding reduces ear infection risk in infants
Recurrent ear infections need ENT specialist referral — may need grommets

see_doctor_if: Any discharge from the ear
Hearing loss that persists after infection resolves
Fever above 39°C with ear pain
Pain behind the ear or swelling behind the ear — mastoiditis (serious)
Symptoms not improving after 48 hours of antibiotics
ear_infection.local_context: Ear infections are one of the most common reasons Ugandan children see a doctor. Untreated or recurrent ear infections are a leading cause of preventable hearing loss and school difficulties in children. Take ear infections seriously.
home_remedies: Warm compress — wet cloth in warm water, wring out, hold against ear
Garlic oil — traditional antibacterial drop: warm garlic-infused olive oil, 2 drops in ear
Onion poultice — traditional remedy: warm sliced onion held against ear
Breast milk drops — contains antibodies, traditional remedy for infant ear infections

common_cold.name: Common Cold
common_cold.description: A viral infection of the upper respiratory tract caused by rhinovirus and other viruses. The most common illness in the world. Causes runny nose, sneezing, mild sore throat, and mild fever. Self-limiting — resolves in 7-10 days.
common_cold.body_mechanism: Cold viruses infect the cells lining your nose and throat. Your immune system responds by triggering inflammation — causing the nasal lining to swell and produce extra mucus (runny nose, congestion). Sneezing is the body's mechanism to expel viruses. The mild fever is the immune system raising body temperature to kill viruses. Antibiotics do nothing — colds are viral.

immediate: Rest — your body needs energy to fight the virus
Drink plenty of warm fluids — loosens mucus and prevents dehydration
Honey and lemon in warm water — soothes throat and provides energy
Steam inhalation — loosens congestion
Saline nasal drops — helps clear the nose gently
short_term: Paracetamol or ibuprofen for fever and sore throat — not for the cold itself
Do NOT take antibiotics — they do not work against viruses and cause harm
Vitamin C foods — oranges, tomatoes, guavas — support immune recovery
Zinc lozenges can reduce cold duration if taken early
Most colds resolve completely in 7-10 days without treatment
long_term: Wash hands frequently — colds spread through hand contact mostly
Avoid touching your face — virus enters through nose and eyes
Good sleep and nutrition — keeps immune system strong
Stay home when sick — consider others around you

see_doctor_if: Fever above 39°C lasting more than 3 days
Severe headache or facial pain — possible sinusitis
Breathlessness or chest pain — possible pneumonia
Symptoms lasting more than 10-14 days without improvement
Worsening after initial improvement — bacterial superinfection
common_cold.local_context: Cold viruses circulate year-round in Uganda but peak during cooler periods. Most Ugandans treat colds with antibiotics — this is unnecessary, creates drug resistance, and has real side effects. Rest, fluids, and symptom management are all that is needed.
home_remedies: Ginger, lemon, and honey tea — the most effective traditional cold remedy
Steam with eucalyptus — decongestant and antimicrobial
Onion and garlic in soup — traditional immune support with some scientific backing
Warm fluids of any kind — the single most important home treatment

measles.name: Measles
measles.description: A highly contagious viral disease causing fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes, and a characteristic spreading rash. Preventable by vaccine. Can cause serious complications including pneumonia, brain damage, and blindness — especially in malnourished children.
measles.body_mechanism: The measles virus spreads through the air and infects the respiratory tract. It then spreads through the bloodstream to skin, eyes, and the rest of the body. The characteristic rash begins on the face and spreads downward — caused by immune cells attacking virus-infected skin cells. Measles also temporarily paralyses the immune system for 2-3 years after recovery, making the child vulnerable to other infections.

immediate: Isolate from other children and unvaccinated people immediately — measles is highly contagious
Take to health facility for confirmation and vitamin A treatment
Paracetamol for fever — never aspirin in children
Maintain hydration — measles causes high fever and poor appetite
Keep eyes clean — wipe gently with clean damp cloth
short_term: Vitamin A supplementation — given at health facilities, dramatically reduces complications
Nutritious food and fluids — malnutrition dramatically worsens measles outcomes
Monitor for complications — ear infection, pneumonia, diarrhoea
Eye care — keep eyes clean, avoid bright light if sensitive
Complete rest for 1-2 weeks
long_term: Vaccination is the only prevention — ensure all children receive 2 doses of MMR vaccine
Check vaccination status of all family members
Measles outbreaks require notification of health authorities
Children after measles recovery need extra nutrition for 3 months — immune system rebuilding

see_doctor_if: Any suspected measles — needs vitamin A at health facility immediately
Breathing difficulty — possible pneumonia complication
Eye discharge or inability to open eyes
Ear pain — ear infection complication
Confusion or seizures — very serious, go immediately
measles.local_context: Measles outbreaks occur regularly in unvaccinated communities in Uganda. The vaccine is free. A child who gets measles in Uganda may recover but is then immune-suppressed for 2-3 years — becoming vulnerable to malaria, TB, and pneumonia. Vaccination protects far more than just against measles.
home_remedies: Vitamin A — the most important treatment, get it from the health centre immediately
Hydration with ORS or clean water
Moringa leaves — nutritionally dense, supports immune recovery
Keep in a quiet, dimly lit room — measles makes eyes very sensitive to light

hepatitis_b.name: Hepatitis B
hepatitis_b.description: A viral infection of the liver transmitted through blood and body fluids. Most adults clear the infection naturally. Chronic hepatitis B (persisting over 6 months) causes ongoing liver damage, cirrhosis, and liver cancer. Uganda has very high prevalence.
hepatitis_b.body_mechanism: The hepatitis B virus infects liver cells and uses them to replicate. Your immune system attacks infected liver cells — causing inflammation (hepatitis). In most healthy adults, this immune response clears the virus within 6 months. In people infected at birth or in early childhood (very common in Uganda), the immune system fails to clear it, causing chronic infection with ongoing liver cell destruction over decades.

immediate: Get tested at a health facility — HBsAg blood test confirms hepatitis B
Avoid all alcohol completely — it dramatically accelerates liver damage
Do not share needles, razors, or any blood-contact items
Use condoms — hepatitis B is sexually transmitted
Inform close contacts — family members need testing and vaccination
short_term: Enroll in hepatitis B care at a health facility
Liver function tests and hepatitis B DNA level to assess disease activity
Antiviral medication (tenofovir) may be prescribed for active disease
Hepatitis B is not curable but is manageable — treatment prevents liver cancer
All household contacts should be vaccinated if not already
long_term: Regular 6-monthly liver monitoring — liver function tests, ultrasound
Hepatitis B vaccine for all unvaccinated family members — 3 doses
Liver cancer surveillance by ultrasound every 6 months if chronic
Complete alcohol abstinence for life
Antiviral therapy reduces liver cancer risk by 70%

see_doctor_if: Any yellowing of eyes or skin
Severe fatigue with upper right abdominal pain
Vomiting blood — indicates advanced liver disease
Swollen abdomen — indicates ascites (liver failure)
All hepatitis B positive people need specialist monitoring
hepatitis_b.local_context: Uganda has one of the world's highest hepatitis B prevalence rates — up to 10% of the population are chronically infected. Most were infected at birth before widespread vaccination. The hepatitis B vaccine is now part of Uganda's routine infant immunisation — all children should receive it. Treatment is available free at most regional hospitals.
home_remedies: Complete alcohol abstinence — the single most important lifestyle factor
Milk thistle — traditional liver support with some evidence for reducing inflammation
Moringa — nutritional support for liver health
Turmeric — anti-inflammatory support, but cannot replace antiviral treatment

gout.name: Gout
gout.description: A form of inflammatory arthritis caused by excess uric acid forming crystals in joints. Causes sudden, severe joint pain — most often in the big toe — with redness, swelling, and warmth. Triggers include alcohol, red meat, and certain medications.
gout.body_mechanism: Uric acid is a breakdown product of purines — found in red meat, organ meat, beer, and shellfish. Normally excreted by the kidneys, in gout either too much is produced or too little is excreted. When uric acid accumulates, it forms needle-shaped crystals that deposit in joint fluid. White blood cells attack the crystals, causing intense inflammation — the gouty attack.

immediate: Rest the affected joint — do not walk on a painful gouty foot
Elevate the affected limb above heart level to reduce swelling
Apply ice pack wrapped in cloth — 20 minutes on, 20 off
Take ibuprofen or diclofenac at maximum dose — most effective for gout attack
Drink large amounts of water — helps flush uric acid through kidneys
short_term: See doctor — colchicine is very effective for acute gout and needs prescription
Completely avoid alcohol, especially beer and spirits — most potent trigger
Avoid red meat, organ meat (liver, kidney), shellfish during attack
Continue hydration — aim for 2-3 litres of water daily
Attack usually resolves completely within 3-10 days with treatment
long_term: Allopurinol — daily medication to lower uric acid — discuss with doctor after 2nd attack
Lose excess weight — obesity dramatically increases uric acid
Limit alcohol, red meat, and high-purine foods permanently
Stay very well hydrated daily — prevents crystal formation
Some blood pressure medications raise uric acid — discuss alternatives with doctor

see_doctor_if: First ever severe joint attack — confirm it is gout not septic arthritis
Fever with joint pain — infection in joint is an emergency
Multiple joint attacks per year — needs long-term uric acid treatment
Kidney stones alongside gout — high uric acid affects kidneys too
gout.local_context: Gout is increasing in Uganda with dietary changes — more red meat, beer, and soda consumption. It is often confused with septic arthritis (infected joint) — the difference is that gout is usually not associated with fever and occurs in the big toe characteristically. Both need medical assessment.
home_remedies: Cherry juice or fresh cherries — has good evidence for reducing uric acid and attack frequency
Large amounts of water — the most important preventive measure
Complete avoidance of alcohol — especially beer
Lemon juice in water — alkalinises urine, helps excrete uric acid

chickenpox.name: Chickenpox (Varicella)
chickenpox.description: A highly contagious viral infection causing an itchy, blister-like rash all over the body, fever, and fatigue. Usually mild in healthy children but can be severe in adults and immunocompromised people. The virus stays in the body for life and can reactivate as shingles decades later.
chickenpox.body_mechanism: The varicella-zoster virus spreads through the air and direct contact. It infects the skin cells and causes the characteristic blisters — each blister contains live virus. The rash progresses through stages: red spots, fluid-filled blisters, crusting over. Different stages appear simultaneously on the body. The virus then retreats into nerve cells where it remains dormant for life.

immediate: Isolate from school, work, and public until ALL blisters have crusted over — usually 7 days
Cut fingernails short and keep hands clean — scratching causes scarring and infection
Apply calamine lotion or 1% hydrocortisone cream to blisters — reduces itch
Antihistamine tablet — reduces itch significantly
Cool bath with oatmeal or baking soda — soothes inflamed skin
short_term: Paracetamol for fever — NEVER aspirin in children (Reye's syndrome risk)
Loose, cool, cotton clothing — reduces skin irritation
Keep blisters clean and dry — prevents bacterial superinfection
In adults or immunocompromised — antiviral (aciclovir) within 24 hours of rash significantly reduces severity
Monitor for complications — bacterial infection of blisters, pneumonia, encephalitis
long_term: Once recovered, lifelong immunity against chickenpox
Virus remains in body — can reactivate as shingles (painful rash) in later life
Vaccinate non-immune close contacts to prevent future cases
Shingles vaccine available for adults over 50 to prevent reactivation

see_doctor_if: Any adult with chickenpox — more likely to need antivirals
Blisters that look infected — red, warm, painful, with pus
Difficulty breathing or chest pain
Severe headache or confusion — possible brain involvement
Chickenpox in a pregnant woman — affects unborn baby
chickenpox.local_context: Chickenpox is very common in Ugandan schools and spreads rapidly in classroom settings. Most children recover completely. The calamine lotion and antihistamine approach is very effective. Adults who have never had chickenpox should be aware they will likely get a more severe illness than children.
home_remedies: Oat bath — ground oats in lukewarm water, soak 15 minutes, excellent for itch
Calamine lotion — traditional and highly effective for itch relief
Neem leaf bath — antiviral properties, traditional remedy with some evidence
Baking soda paste — apply to particularly itchy spots for quick relief

epilepsy.name: Epilepsy / Seizure Disorder
epilepsy.description: A neurological condition causing recurrent, unprovoked seizures — sudden abnormal electrical activity in the brain. Affects 1-2% of people. Most people with epilepsy live full lives with appropriate medication. Uganda has high prevalence partly due to birth complications and infections.
epilepsy.body_mechanism: The brain communicates through electrical signals between neurons. In epilepsy, groups of neurons fire abnormally and synchronously — like an electrical storm. This can cause loss of consciousness, muscle convulsions, blank staring, or brief confusion depending on which area of the brain is affected. Between seizures, the brain functions normally.

immediate: During a seizure — do NOT hold the person down, do NOT put anything in their mouth
Clear the area of anything dangerous — move furniture, sharp objects away
Turn the person on their side — prevents choking if they vomit
Time the seizure — most end within 2-3 minutes
Stay with the person and reassure them calmly when they regain consciousness
short_term: See a neurologist or doctor for formal diagnosis after first seizure
Seizures lasting more than 5 minutes or multiple seizures without recovery — call for help immediately
Identify and avoid triggers — sleep deprivation, alcohol, flashing lights, stress
Take anti-epileptic medication exactly as prescribed — never skip doses
Carry medical ID stating epilepsy diagnosis and medications
long_term: Most people achieve seizure control with appropriate medication
Never stop anti-epileptic medication without doctor's guidance — this triggers dangerous breakthrough seizures
Some activities are restricted — no swimming alone, no operating heavy machinery until seizure-free for 2 years
Pregnancy requires specialist monitoring — some epilepsy drugs affect the baby
Protect yourself — wear helmet when cycling, shower rather than bath

see_doctor_if: First ever seizure — always needs medical evaluation
Seizure lasting more than 5 minutes — status epilepticus, call for emergency help immediately
Seizures increasing in frequency despite medication
Injury during a seizure
Seizures during pregnancy
epilepsy.local_context: Epilepsy is particularly common in Uganda — up to 5 times the global average — partly due to birth complications, neonatal infections, and neurocysticercosis (pork tapeworm larvae in the brain, preventable by not eating undercooked pork). Epilepsy is NOT caused by witchcraft or spiritual forces — it is a brain condition with effective medical treatment. Stigma prevents many Ugandans from seeking care.
home_remedies: There is no home remedy for epilepsy — medical treatment is essential
Consistent medication is the most effective treatment
Sleep adequately — sleep deprivation is the most common seizure trigger
Avoid alcohol — lowers seizure threshold significantly

typhoid_complications.name: Enteric Fever / Complicated Typhoid
typhoid_complications.description: Severe typhoid fever with complications — intestinal perforation, haemorrhage, or typhoid encephalopathy. Life-threatening medical emergency requiring surgical management.
typhoid_complications.body_mechanism: In complicated typhoid, Salmonella typhi bacteria penetrate and destroy the intestinal wall — causing perforation (a hole in the gut). Intestinal contents spill into the abdominal cavity causing peritonitis — a life-threatening infection. The toxins can also affect the brain causing typhoid encephalopathy. Bleeding from the intestine can cause haemorrhage.

immediate: Go to hospital immediately — this may require emergency surgery
Do not eat or drink anything — NPO (nil by mouth) if perforation suspected
Tell the doctor how many days you have had the fever
IV antibiotics and surgery for perforation are the treatments
Do not take painkillers that may mask the signs needed for surgical assessment
short_term: Surgery if intestinal perforation confirmed
IV antibiotics — ciprofloxacin or ceftriaxone
Intensive hospital monitoring
Nutritional support via IV or feeding tube post-surgery
long_term: Full recovery possible with prompt treatment
Maintain strict food and water hygiene to prevent recurrence
Typhoid vaccination for prevention
Family members need stool testing to identify carriers

see_doctor_if: Sudden severe abdominal pain in a typhoid patient — possible perforation, emergency
Confusion or altered consciousness in typhoid
High fever lasting more than 7-10 days without improvement on antibiotics
Vomiting blood or blood in stool with typhoid
typhoid_complications.local_context: Intestinal perforation from typhoid is a major surgical emergency in Uganda, particularly in patients who present late or are partially treated. Any typhoid patient whose pain suddenly gets dramatically worse needs emergency surgical evaluation.
home_remedies: No home remedies — surgical emergency requires hospital care
Previous home treatment of typhoid with partial antibiotic courses increases perforation risk

osteoarthritis.name: Osteoarthritis
osteoarthritis.description: A degenerative joint condition where the cartilage cushioning the ends of bones gradually wears down. Causes joint pain, stiffness, and reduced range of motion — particularly in knees, hips, and hands. The most common form of arthritis, increasing with age.
osteoarthritis.body_mechanism: Cartilage is the smooth tissue covering the ends of bones in joints — it allows smooth, pain-free movement. In osteoarthritis, this cartilage gradually breaks down over decades of use, trauma, or excess weight load. Without cartilage cushioning, bone rubs on bone — causing pain, inflammation, and the formation of bone spurs (osteophytes). The pain is worse with activity and improves with rest.

immediate: Rest the affected joint from activities that worsen pain
Apply heat to stiff joints before activity — improves mobility
Apply ice after activity to reduce inflammation
Ibuprofen or diclofenac for pain and inflammation
Gentle range-of-motion exercises even when in pain — immobility worsens osteoarthritis
short_term: Start a gentle daily exercise program — walking, swimming, or cycling
Weight loss if overweight — every 1kg lost reduces knee joint load by 4kg
Paracetamol for mild pain, ibuprofen with food for moderate pain
Physiotherapy referral for exercise prescription and joint protection strategies
Knee supports and appropriate footwear reduce joint load
long_term: Consistent gentle exercise is the most evidence-based treatment for osteoarthritis
Weight management — the single most modifiable risk factor
Glucosamine and chondroitin supplements — modest evidence, widely used
Joint replacement surgery for severe cases — highly effective for hip and knee
Adapt activities — reduce high-impact exercise, increase low-impact alternatives

see_doctor_if: Severe pain preventing walking or daily activities
Sudden worsening — possible joint infection or fracture
Significant joint swelling, warmth, or redness — may be different type of arthritis
Considering surgery — needs specialist orthopaedic assessment
osteoarthritis.local_context: Osteoarthritis is increasingly common in older Ugandans, particularly affecting knees from years of manual labour, carrying heavy loads, and farming. Many Ugandans present late when the joint is severely damaged. Weight management and exercise remain the most effective interventions at any stage.
home_remedies: Warm turmeric milk — curcumin has anti-inflammatory properties
Gentle warm salt water soaks for hand osteoarthritis
Ginger tea — natural anti-inflammatory
Neem oil massage — traditional anti-inflammatory joint treatment

syphilis.name: Syphilis
syphilis.description: A bacterial sexually transmitted infection caused by Treponema pallidum. Highly curable with antibiotics but causes serious complications if untreated. Dangerous in pregnancy — can cause stillbirth and birth defects.
syphilis.body_mechanism: The Treponema pallidum bacteria enters through mucous membranes or skin breaks during sexual contact. It spreads through the bloodstream to all organs. Without treatment it progresses through four stages over years, eventually damaging the heart, brain, and nervous system.

immediate: Go to a health facility immediately — syphilis is completely curable with penicillin
Avoid all sexual contact until you and your partner(s) have been tested and treated
If pregnant, go to hospital urgently — syphilis in pregnancy can kill the baby
short_term: Complete the full penicillin treatment course as prescribed
Notify all recent sexual partners so they can be tested and treated
Test for HIV — syphilis significantly increases HIV transmission risk
long_term: Re-test at 3 months and 12 months to confirm cure
Use condoms consistently to prevent reinfection
Annual STI screening if sexually active with multiple partners

see_doctor_if: You have any painless sore on genitals, mouth, or anus
You have a rash on your palms or soles of feet
You are pregnant and have not been tested for syphilis
You had unprotected sex with someone who may have syphilis
syphilis.local_context: Syphilis is common in Uganda and is tested at all antenatal clinics — all pregnant women should be screened. The test is a simple blood test (VDRL/RPR). Treatment with penicillin is free at government facilities. Many people have syphilis without knowing it.

gonorrhoea.name: Gonorrhoea
gonorrhoea.description: A common bacterial sexually transmitted infection caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Very common in Uganda. Highly treatable but drug-resistant strains are increasing. A major cause of infertility if untreated.
gonorrhoea.body_mechanism: The bacteria infect the mucous membranes of the urethra, cervix, rectum, throat, and eyes. In women, it can spread to the fallopian tubes causing pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), which scars the tubes and causes infertility or ectopic pregnancy.

immediate: Go to a health facility — gonorrhoea requires specific antibiotics, do not self-treat
Do not have sex until you and your partner have both completed treatment
Test for HIV and other STIs at the same visit
short_term: Take the full antibiotic course — even if symptoms clear after a day or two
Ensure your partner is also treated — reinfection from an untreated partner is very common
Return for follow-up test 1 week after treatment to confirm cure
long_term: Use condoms consistently
Annual STI screening if sexually active with new or multiple partners

see_doctor_if: Yellow, green, or pus-like discharge from penis or vagina
Burning or pain when urinating
Pelvic or lower abdominal pain in women
Swollen or painful testicles
You had unprotected sex with someone who has gonorrhoea
gonorrhoea.local_context: Gonorrhoea is among the most common STIs in Uganda. Drug resistance is increasing — never self-treat with leftover antibiotics. Treatment is free at government health facilities. Both partners must be treated simultaneously.

chlamydia.name: Chlamydia
chlamydia.description: The most common bacterial STI worldwide, caused by Chlamydia trachomatis. Often called the 'silent infection' because most people have no symptoms. A leading preventable cause of infertility in women.
chlamydia.body_mechanism: Infects cervical and urethral cells. In women, bacteria can ascend to infect the fallopian tubes (PID), causing scarring that blocks eggs from reaching the uterus, leading to infertility or ectopic pregnancy. In men, can cause epididymitis. Easily passed from mother to baby during birth causing eye infections and pneumonia in newborns.

immediate: Go to a health facility for testing and treatment — azithromycin or doxycycline are effective
Inform recent sexual partners so they can be tested and treated
Test for HIV, gonorrhoea, and syphilis at the same visit
short_term: Complete the full antibiotic course
Avoid sex for 1 week after single-dose treatment, or until 7-day course is complete
Both partners must be treated simultaneously
long_term: Re-test 3 months after treatment — reinfection is common
Annual chlamydia screening for all sexually active people under 25

see_doctor_if: Unusual discharge from genitals
Burning when urinating
Pelvic pain or pain during sex
Irregular bleeding between periods
Swollen or painful testicles
You are pregnant — chlamydia can harm the baby
chlamydia.local_context: Chlamydia testing is available at most Uganda health facilities. Many people infected with chlamydia have no symptoms at all — which is why it silently causes infertility. If you have been sexually active with new partners, get tested even without symptoms.

herpes_genital.name: Genital Herpes (HSV-2)
herpes_genital.description: A lifelong viral infection caused by Herpes Simplex Virus type 2 (HSV-2). Very common — most infected people don't know they have it. While incurable, antiviral medications significantly reduce outbreaks and transmission risk.
herpes_genital.body_mechanism: After initial infection, HSV-2 hides in nerve ganglia at the base of the spine and periodically reactivates, causing sores on the genitals, buttocks, or thighs. Transmission occurs through skin-to-skin contact — condoms reduce but don't eliminate risk. Most transmission happens when no sores are visible.

immediate: See a health worker for diagnosis — acyclovir reduces severity if started early in the first outbreak
Keep sores clean and dry
Avoid sexual contact during outbreaks — this is when transmission risk is highest
short_term: Daily antiviral medication (acyclovir 400mg twice daily) suppresses outbreaks and reduces transmission
Use condoms consistently — reduces but does not eliminate transmission risk
Inform partners — they have a right to know
long_term: Most people have fewer and milder outbreaks over time
Triggers: stress, illness, fatigue, menstruation — managing these reduces outbreaks
If pregnant: tell your doctor — antiviral treatment prevents passing herpes to the baby during birth

see_doctor_if: First outbreak — get proper diagnosis and antiviral treatment
Outbreaks happening more than 6 times per year
You are pregnant
Sores are very painful or spreading
You develop fever, stiff neck, or difficulty urinating
herpes_genital.local_context: Herpes is very common in Uganda but rarely discussed openly. It is a manageable chronic condition — not a life sentence. Acyclovir is available at pharmacies. Many people with herpes live completely normal lives, including having children safely.
home_remedies: Cool water compresses soothe discomfort during outbreaks
Keep sores clean and dry — loose cotton underwear helps
Avoid tight clothing during outbreaks

cervical_cancer.name: Cervical Cancer
cervical_cancer.description: Cancer of the cervix (the lower part of the uterus). The leading cancer killer of Ugandan women. Caused almost entirely by Human Papillomavirus (HPV). 100% preventable with vaccination and early detection through screening.
cervical_cancer.body_mechanism: HPV virus infects cervical cells, causing mutations that over 10-15 years can progress from pre-cancerous changes to invasive cancer. This slow progression means screening can catch it before it becomes cancer. Once invasive, cancer cells can spread to surrounding tissues, lymph nodes, and other organs.

immediate: If you have any of these symptoms, see a health worker urgently
All women aged 25–65 should have a cervical cancer screen — VIA test is free at government facilities
If you have not been screened in the last 3 years, go today
short_term: Treatment depends on stage — early stages are curable with surgery, radiation, or cryotherapy
Treatment is available at regional referral hospitals and Mulago in Uganda
Support groups available at Uganda Cancer Institute, Kampala
long_term: After treatment: follow-up every 3-6 months for 2 years, then annually
HPV vaccination of daughters aged 9-14 — prevents the virus that causes this cancer
Continue cervical screening even after HPV vaccination

see_doctor_if: Bleeding after sex — this is the classic early warning sign of cervical cancer
Bleeding between periods or after menopause
Unusual or foul-smelling vaginal discharge
Pelvic or low back pain
You have never had a cervical cancer screen — go now regardless of symptoms
cervical_cancer.local_context: Cervical cancer kills more Ugandan women than any other cancer. It is ENTIRELY PREVENTABLE. Free VIA (visual inspection with acetic acid) screening is available at all health centre IVs and hospitals. HPV vaccination is part of Uganda's school vaccination programme for girls aged 10. The Uganda Cancer Institute in Mulago offers treatment.

breast_cancer.name: Breast Cancer
breast_cancer.description: Cancer originating in breast tissue. The most common cancer in women worldwide. Early detection through breast self-examination and clinical examination dramatically improves survival — most early-stage breast cancers are curable.
breast_cancer.body_mechanism: Breast cells acquire mutations (sometimes inherited — BRCA genes, sometimes random) that cause uncontrolled growth. A tumour forms, which if undetected can spread through lymph nodes to other organs (bone, lung, liver, brain). Early detection before spread is the key to survival.

immediate: Any new breast lump must be assessed by a health worker — do not wait and see
Go to the nearest health facility or hospital with a surgical unit
Early detection saves lives — do not delay
short_term: Diagnosis requires examination, ultrasound, and biopsy
Treatment depends on type and stage: surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, hormonal therapy
Uganda Cancer Institute, Mulago: 0800-100-004
long_term: Breast self-examination monthly — best done 7-10 days after period starts
Clinical breast examination annually from age 30
Know your family history — BRCA gene mutations run in families
prevention: Breastfeed for at least 1 year — reduces breast cancer risk by 20-30%

see_doctor_if: Any new breast lump — even if not painful, even in young women
Any change in breast shape or skin
Nipple discharge (especially blood-stained)
Nipple turning inward
Swelling or thickening of breast skin
breast_cancer.local_context: Breast cancer incidence is rising in Uganda. Many women present late because they fear the diagnosis or lack access to care. The Uganda Cancer Institute provides subsidised treatment. The Cancer Institute helpline is 0800-100-004 (free call). Do monthly self-examination and report any lump immediately.

prostate_cancer.name: Prostate Cancer
prostate_cancer.description: Cancer of the prostate gland. The most common cancer in men worldwide. Often grows slowly. Risk increases dramatically with age — mainly affects men over 50. African men have the highest global risk.
prostate_cancer.body_mechanism: The prostate gland surrounds the urethra. Cancer cells grow uncontrolled, enlarging the prostate and blocking urinary flow. Advanced cancer can spread to bones (causing bone pain) and lymph nodes.

immediate: Men over 50 with urinary symptoms should see a health worker for PSA blood test and examination
Do not ignore urinary symptoms — early prostate cancer is very treatable
short_term: Diagnosis: PSA blood test + digital rectal examination + biopsy
Treatment options range from watchful waiting (slow-growing) to surgery, radiotherapy, or hormonal therapy
long_term: Men of African descent should discuss screening with a doctor from age 40
Annual PSA testing from age 50 (age 40 if African ancestry or family history)

see_doctor_if: Difficulty starting or stopping urination
Weak urine stream
Need to urinate very frequently, especially at night
Blood in urine or semen
Bone pain in back, hips, or thighs in a man over 50
prostate_cancer.local_context: African men have the highest global risk of prostate cancer. The Uganda Cancer Institute performs PSA testing. Many Ugandan men delay seeking care — early detection dramatically improves outcomes. Any man over 50 with urinary symptoms should be checked.

hypothyroidism.name: Hypothyroidism (Underactive Thyroid)
hypothyroidism.description: The thyroid gland in the neck doesn't produce enough thyroid hormone, slowing down the body's metabolism. Very common, especially in women. Often missed because symptoms are vague and develop slowly. Completely treatable with a daily tablet.
hypothyroidism.body_mechanism: Thyroid hormone controls the speed of every cell in the body — metabolism, heart rate, brain function, body temperature. When levels fall, everything slows: heart rate drops, metabolism slows causing weight gain, brain function dulls causing brain fog and depression, body cools causing feeling cold all the time.

immediate: See a health worker for thyroid blood tests (TSH and T4) — a simple blood test diagnoses this
Do not self-diagnose based on symptoms alone — these symptoms overlap with many conditions
short_term: Treatment: levothyroxine (synthetic thyroid hormone) — taken once daily on empty stomach
Symptoms usually improve within 4-8 weeks of starting treatment
Take medication at the same time every day — consistency matters
long_term: Lifelong daily medication is usually required
Annual blood tests to check thyroid hormone levels and adjust dose
Most people on correct dose live completely normal lives with no symptoms

see_doctor_if: Unexplained weight gain despite not eating more
Constant fatigue that sleep doesn't fix
Feeling cold when others are comfortable
Increasing depression or brain fog
Neck swelling — may indicate goitre
Very heavy periods in women
hypothyroidism.local_context: Iodine deficiency — historically common in Uganda's inland areas — can cause hypothyroidism and goitre. Iodised salt has helped but deficiency still exists. Women are 5-8 times more likely than men to develop hypothyroidism. Levothyroxine is available at government facilities though sometimes in short supply.
home_remedies: Ensure you use iodised salt — iodine is essential for thyroid function
Selenium-rich foods (sunflower seeds, mushrooms) support thyroid function
Avoid raw cruciferous vegetables in very large amounts if iodine-deficient

hyperthyroidism.name: Hyperthyroidism (Overactive Thyroid)
hyperthyroidism.description: The thyroid gland produces too much thyroid hormone, speeding up the body's metabolism. Causes rapid heart rate, weight loss despite eating well, heat intolerance, and anxiety. Most commonly caused by Graves' disease (an autoimmune condition).
hyperthyroidism.body_mechanism: Excess thyroid hormone accelerates every bodily process — heart beats faster (sometimes causing dangerous arrhythmias), metabolism speeds up (causing weight loss and heat production), nervous system is overstimulated (causing anxiety, tremors, insomnia).

immediate: See a health worker urgently if you have rapid irregular heartbeat with thyroid symptoms — risk of stroke
Blood tests (TSH, T3, T4) confirm diagnosis
short_term: Treatment options: antithyroid drugs (carbimazole), beta-blockers for heart rate control, radioactive iodine therapy, or surgery
Avoid iodine-rich foods and supplements during treatment
long_term: Treatment often leads to remission or cured state
Some patients develop hypothyroidism after treatment and require levothyroxine
Regular monitoring of thyroid levels is essential

see_doctor_if: Rapid or irregular heartbeat
Unexplained weight loss despite eating normally
Bulging eyes (Graves' ophthalmopathy)
Neck swelling
Severe anxiety or tremors
hyperthyroidism.local_context: Hyperthyroidism is less common than hypothyroidism in Uganda but important to diagnose. Neck swelling (goitre) may indicate thyroid disease — see a health worker for any neck swelling. Carbimazole for treatment is available at regional hospitals.

pcos.name: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
pcos.description: A hormonal disorder affecting women of reproductive age. Characterised by irregular periods, excess male hormones (causing acne and excess hair), and small fluid-filled sacs (cysts) on the ovaries. The most common cause of female infertility. Very underdiagnosed.
pcos.body_mechanism: The ovaries produce excess androgens (male hormones). High insulin levels (insulin resistance is very common in PCOS) stimulate androgen production. High androgens prevent normal ovulation — eggs partially develop then don't release, forming small cysts. No ovulation means no regular periods and difficulty getting pregnant.

immediate: See a gynaecologist for diagnosis — diagnosis requires 2 of 3 criteria: irregular periods, signs of high androgens, ovarian cysts on ultrasound
short_term: Weight loss of even 5% significantly improves hormonal balance and restores periods
Low glycaemic diet and exercise improve insulin resistance
Medication: metformin (improves insulin resistance), combined pill (regulates periods, reduces acne/hair)
long_term: PCOS increases lifetime risk of diabetes, hypertension, and endometrial cancer — management is long-term
For fertility: clomifene or letrozole stimulate ovulation
Annual blood glucose and blood pressure checks

see_doctor_if: Irregular or absent periods
Difficulty getting pregnant
Excess facial or body hair
Severe acne not responding to treatment
Unexplained weight gain around the abdomen
pcos.local_context: PCOS is very common — affecting 1 in 10 women worldwide — but massively underdiagnosed in Uganda. Many women are told they are 'barren' without ever receiving a PCOS diagnosis. Gynaecological services are available at all regional hospitals. Metformin (used to treat PCOS) is available free at government facilities.
home_remedies: Regular exercise — 30 minutes daily dramatically improves PCOS symptoms
Low glycaemic diet — reduce sugar, white rice, refined carbohydrates
Spearmint tea may reduce androgen levels (limited evidence but safe)
Cinnamon has some evidence for improving insulin sensitivity in PCOS

endometriosis.name: Endometriosis
endometriosis.description: A condition where tissue similar to the uterine lining grows outside the uterus — on ovaries, fallopian tubes, bowel, or bladder. Causes severe pain, heavy periods, and infertility. Often takes 7-10 years to diagnose because pain is normalised. Affects 1 in 10 women.
endometriosis.body_mechanism: The misplaced endometrial-like tissue responds to hormonal cycles just like normal uterine lining — it thickens, breaks down, and bleeds each month. But unlike normal menstrual blood, this bleeding has nowhere to go, causing inflammation, scarring, and cysts (endometriomas on ovaries). Scar tissue can glue organs together.

immediate: See a gynaecologist — do not accept that severe period pain is 'normal'
Pain that stops you going to school, work, or your daily activities is NOT normal period pain
short_term: Pain management: ibuprofen (take before pain starts, not when severe), hormonal therapies
Hormonal treatment: combined pill, progestogen-only pill, or hormonal IUS — all reduce endometriosis activity
Heat pad on abdomen and lower back during pain
long_term: Definitive diagnosis requires laparoscopy (surgery) — but treatment can be started based on symptoms
Surgical treatment removes endometriosis deposits
Endometriosis improves after menopause but requires long-term management
Fertility treatment may be needed — see a reproductive specialist

see_doctor_if: Period pain severe enough to miss school, work, or social activities
Pain during sex
Pain when passing urine or bowel movements during period
Very heavy periods
Unable to get pregnant after trying for 12 months
endometriosis.local_context: Endometriosis is severely underdiagnosed in Uganda. Many women are told their severe period pain is normal, or that they must simply 'endure it'. Period pain that is disabling is NOT normal and deserves investigation. Gynaecological assessment is available at regional hospitals and Mulago.
home_remedies: Heat therapy — hot water bottle on abdomen and lower back reduces muscle cramping
Ibuprofen taken BEFORE pain peaks is more effective than waiting
Anti-inflammatory diet (reduce processed foods, increase vegetables and omega-3 rich fish)

uterine_fibroids.name: Uterine Fibroids
uterine_fibroids.description: Non-cancerous muscular growths in or around the uterus. Extremely common — up to 80% of women will have fibroids by age 50. African women are disproportionately affected. Most fibroids cause no symptoms but large ones cause heavy bleeding, pelvic pain, and infertility.
uterine_fibroids.body_mechanism: Fibroids (leiomyomas) are benign tumours of uterine smooth muscle. They are oestrogen-sensitive and grow during reproductive years, shrinking after menopause. Their location determines symptoms: those inside the uterine cavity cause heavy bleeding; those pressing on the bladder cause urinary frequency; large fibroids distort the uterus causing infertility.

immediate: See a gynaecologist for pelvic examination and ultrasound to diagnose fibroids
If bleeding is very heavy causing dizziness, go to hospital urgently — severe anaemia risk
short_term: Treat associated anaemia with iron supplements
Pain: ibuprofen or mefenamic acid for period pain
Hormonal treatment reduces bleeding: progestogens, hormonal IUS
GnRH analogues shrink fibroids temporarily before surgery
long_term: Surgical options: myomectomy (removes fibroids, preserves uterus — for those wanting pregnancy), hysterectomy (definitive cure)
UAE (uterine artery embolisation) — available in major hospitals
Fibroids usually shrink naturally after menopause

see_doctor_if: Very heavy periods (soaking more than 1 pad per hour)
Periods lasting more than 7 days
Visible abdominal swelling
Difficulty getting pregnant
Frequent urination or difficulty emptying bladder
Severe pelvic pain
uterine_fibroids.local_context: Fibroids are extremely common in Ugandan and African women — much more common than in European women due to genetic factors. Many women suffer for years before seeking care. Pelvic ultrasound for fibroid diagnosis is available at most district hospitals. Surgical treatment is available at regional referral hospitals.
home_remedies: Iron-rich foods and iron supplements to manage anaemia from heavy bleeding
Heat pad for period pain relief
Exercise reduces oestrogen levels which may slow fibroid growth

ectopic_pregnancy.name: Ectopic Pregnancy
ectopic_pregnancy.description: A pregnancy that implants outside the uterus — usually in a fallopian tube. A life-threatening emergency. The tube can rupture causing massive internal bleeding. Every woman of reproductive age with abdominal pain must be considered for this.
ectopic_pregnancy.body_mechanism: A fertilised egg cannot reach the uterus (usually due to fallopian tube damage from previous PID/STI) and implants in the tube. The embryo grows, eventually rupturing the tube. Rupture causes rapid internal haemorrhage — a woman can die within hours without emergency surgery.

immediate: EMERGENCY — Go to hospital immediately if you have abdominal pain and a missed period
Call for help — this is life-threatening if the tube ruptures
Do NOT eat or drink anything — you may need emergency surgery
short_term: Treatment: surgery (laparoscopy or open) to remove the ectopic pregnancy
Blood transfusion may be needed if significant blood loss
Follow-up with gynaecologist to assess remaining tube function
long_term: Increased risk of future ectopic pregnancy — early ultrasound essential in subsequent pregnancies
Treat and prevent STIs which damage fallopian tubes

see_doctor_if: Any woman with missed period AND abdominal or pelvic pain — GO TO HOSPITAL NOW
Pain in shoulder tip with abdominal pain and missed period (blood under diaphragm from rupture)
Fainting or collapse with known or possible pregnancy
ectopic_pregnancy.local_context: Ectopic pregnancy is a leading cause of maternal death in Uganda. Previous pelvic inflammatory disease (from gonorrhoea or chlamydia) significantly increases risk by scarring the fallopian tubes. Any woman of reproductive age with abdominal pain must be assessed for ectopic pregnancy.

copd.name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
copd.description: A progressive lung disease causing irreversible narrowing of airways and destruction of air sacs. The leading cause of breathing disability worldwide. In Uganda, primarily caused by biomass fuel smoke (cooking on open fires or charcoal), not just cigarettes.
copd.body_mechanism: Chronic irritant exposure (smoke, dust) causes permanent inflammation and structural damage to airways and alveoli (air sacs). Airways narrow and mucus production increases (chronic bronchitis). Alveoli are destroyed making them less elastic (emphysema). Less air can flow in and out — particularly 'stale' air is trapped, making breathing a constant effort.

immediate: If severe breathlessness or lips turning blue — go to hospital immediately
short_term: Stop smoking and reduce exposure to smoke — this is the single most important action
Salbutamol (blue inhaler) relieves symptoms during breathlessness episodes
Treat all chest infections promptly — they accelerate COPD progression
Pulmonary rehabilitation: supervised breathing exercises improve function significantly
long_term: COPD is not curable but is manageable
Regular inhaler use (both reliever and preventer) if prescribed
Avoid indoor smoke — switch to gas or improved cookstove if possible
Annual influenza vaccination and pneumonia vaccination reduce exacerbations
Oxygen therapy for severe cases

see_doctor_if: Breathlessness that limits daily activities
Chronic cough with phlegm lasting months
Frequent chest infections
Lips or fingertips turning blue
Worsening breathlessness — especially sudden worsening (exacerbation)
copd.local_context: In Uganda, COPD from cooking fire and charcoal smoke is vastly underdiagnosed. Women who cook on open fires for decades are at very high risk. COPD is often mistaken for asthma or TB. Spirometry (lung function test) for diagnosis is available at major hospitals. Salbutamol inhalers are available at most health centres.
home_remedies: Use improved cookstoves or cook outdoors to reduce smoke exposure
Keep home well-ventilated
Breathing exercises: pursed lip breathing (breathe out slowly through puckered lips) reduces breathlessness
Steam inhalation with eucalyptus loosens mucus

chronic_bronchitis.name: Chronic Bronchitis
chronic_bronchitis.description: Persistent inflammation of the bronchial tubes (airways) causing a daily cough with phlegm for at least 3 months in two consecutive years. A form of COPD. Often caused by smoke exposure. Frequently misdiagnosed as TB in Uganda.
chronic_bronchitis.body_mechanism: Chronic irritation causes the mucous glands in airways to enlarge and produce excessive thick mucus. The cilia (hair-like cells that sweep mucus out) are damaged by smoke. Mucus accumulates, causing persistent cough as the body tries to clear it. Airways thicken and narrow, reducing airflow.

immediate: See a health worker — distinguish from TB (which also causes chronic cough) with sputum test
short_term: Stop smoking and reduce smoke exposure — the most important action
Stay well hydrated — thins mucus
Avoid cold air and smoke triggers
Treat respiratory infections promptly
long_term: Reduce cooking fire exposure
Annual influenza vaccination
If breathlessness develops, lung function tests to assess for COPD

see_doctor_if: Cough lasting more than 3 weeks
Blood in phlegm — always needs assessment
Fever with cough — could be pneumonia or TB
Worsening breathlessness
Green or yellow phlegm not improving
chronic_bronchitis.local_context: In Uganda, chronic bronchitis is common due to cooking fire smoke, charcoal, and tobacco. ALWAYS exclude TB with a sputum test before diagnosing chronic bronchitis — TB is endemic and chronic cough is its main symptom.
home_remedies: Steam inhalation 2-3 times daily loosens and thins mucus
Honey and ginger tea soothes airway irritation
Drink at least 8 glasses of water daily to keep mucus thin
Cook outdoors or in well-ventilated spaces

depression_major.name: Major Depressive Disorder
depression_major.description: A serious medical condition causing persistent low mood, loss of interest, and physical symptoms that significantly impair daily functioning. Not sadness — a diagnosable illness involving real changes in brain chemistry. Very common and very treatable.
depression_major.body_mechanism: Depression involves dysregulation of neurotransmitters — serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine — the brain's chemical messengers. The amygdala (fear/emotion centre) becomes overactive while the prefrontal cortex (rational thought) is suppressed. This creates a negative thought bias, emotional numbness, and physical symptoms throughout the body.

immediate: If you have thoughts of harming yourself, tell someone you trust right now or go to a health facility
You are not weak, you are not failing — this is an illness that responds to treatment
short_term: See a health worker — depression is diagnosed clinically and treatment is effective
Antidepressants (amitriptyline, fluoxetine) take 4-6 weeks to work — continue even if you don't feel better immediately
Exercise is as effective as antidepressants for mild-moderate depression — aim for 30 min daily
Reduce alcohol — it is a depressant and worsens depression
long_term: Treatment typically continues for 6-12 months after feeling better
Counselling (CBT) is as effective as medication and reduces relapse
Maintain social connections — isolation worsens depression
Sleep routine is essential — consistent wake times stabilise mood

see_doctor_if: Low mood persisting more than 2 weeks
Loss of interest in everything you used to enjoy
Any thoughts of suicide or self-harm
Unable to work, care for family, or function in daily life
Depression in pregnancy or after childbirth (postpartum depression)
depression_major.local_context: Depression affects 1 in 5 people in Uganda at some point. It is still heavily stigmatised — often seen as spiritual weakness or madness. Mental health care is available at Butabika National Hospital and mental health units at all regional referral hospitals. Amitriptyline and fluoxetine are on the Uganda essential medicines list. Village Health Teams can refer you.
home_remedies: Physical exercise — 30-45 minutes daily of any movement significantly reduces depression symptoms
Social connection — spend time with trusted people even when you don't feel like it
Morning sunlight exposure — regulates circadian rhythms and improves mood
Reduce or stop alcohol

ptsd.name: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD)
ptsd.description: A mental health condition triggered by experiencing or witnessing a terrifying event — war, sexual violence, accidents, natural disasters, or serious injury. The brain becomes stuck in 'survival mode', replaying the trauma. Common in Uganda given conflict history.
ptsd.body_mechanism: Trauma overwhelms the brain's normal processing. The amygdala becomes hypersensitive, treating normal stimuli as threats. Traumatic memories are stored differently — without context of being 'in the past'. Flashbacks, nightmares, and hypervigilance are the brain trying to process what it couldn't at the time of the trauma.

immediate: You are not going mad — PTSD is a normal response to abnormal experiences
Tell someone you trust what you are experiencing
